# 0018. Proofs of all app decisions

**Status:** in progress, 2026-11-07. **Rulings:** VL-9, VL-29. Lane `vl-proveall`.

The proof consumes production VibeLang modules in LemmaScript's plain TypeScript subset, with unchanged `//@`
contracts. Effect shells call those same decisions. The harness discovers every marked module under `src/`,
`worker/` and `scripts/`; omission of an emitted marked function fails. Mutations change executable text only,
strictly typecheck, and must fail a Dafny obligation in their named function. Tool errors never count as rejection,
and neither does a failed precondition at a call. There are no callee-precondition exceptions. A rejection must
be a direct assertion, invariant or postcondition diagnostic in the intended generated file and function; a related
location or another function's failure does not qualify. Every value dependency is freshly proved in the same
invocation, including selected callers and negative runs. Type-only imports carry types, not callable axioms. The
harness rejects unmarked imported contracts and unproved external value modules, and binds imports to source hashes. Rejection shows the contracts detect that change, not that they are
complete. The review's four surviving authorization/action mutants are addressed by the strengthening below.

A proof of these decisions does not prove Effect, Foldkit, HTTP, JSON, the compiler, Dafny/Z3, or Cloudflare.
Unproved logic remains explicitly visible below; a passing gate must never be reported as all functionality proved.

## Gate receipts, first module batch

Baseline: 33 Dafny obligations and 65/65 rejected mutations. This batch: 44 obligations across four production
modules and 84 executable mutations (19 new). The proof gate runs three harness regressions and four inventory
regressions; the inventory gate rejects a stale table. Both proof and mutation targets participate in ordinary CI.
Typechecking passes; 177 unit/integration tests and 13 local workerd tests pass (two opt-in live-model cases skipped).
After rebasing the mythical-history batch, the shared gate proves 63 obligations in five modules and the full suite
passes 203 tests. The original four proof sources and all 84 mutation inputs are unchanged from their green rerun.
The host report records receipts, exits and subsequent batch counts.

## Second module batch

The production gate proves 99 obligations across eight modules. The unchanged implementation of the conversation
machine carries stronger contracts; browser/protocol/mock shells call extracted policies. The unit suite remains
224/224 after the history-page and post/tour-ordering rebases. The browser suite passes 90 local cases after the history-page rebase (six live/deployment cases skipped). The full mutation gate rejects 163/163 executable mutations (79 new), all with unchanged contracts; the full run took 1,075.616 seconds with four workers on the shared host. After the next rebase, all 11 inherited history mutations also reject: 174/174 across the two invocations. Regenerating the full 174-case input set produces byte-identical copies and manifest entries for those receipts.

A mutation-generator defect counted identical text inside the next function's annotations as executable text.
The generator now excludes matches starting in contract lines and preserves multiline assertion anchors. Two
regressions join the harness; every mutation still preserves all contracts byte for byte. Large negative cases name
a specific production postcondition, selected within their function with fail-closed regression tests. Dafny checks
that postcondition in isolation; the positive gate still checks every obligation. Solver timeouts never count as
rejections. The harness now runs seven regressions. Positive batches have a 60-second solver budget; negative cases retain 30 seconds. No timeout counts as a proof or rejection.

uses a proved capacity guard before incrementing the cursor. Runtime schemas admit only safe integer sequences and
ranks, and ranks below their cursor; storage replay, follow rereads and bootstrap validate these boundaries. This
retains all existing mathematical contracts rather than weakening their domains to hide the JavaScript mismatch.

## Sixth module batch: history rank and validated replay

`decide` now specifies the exact append rank (zero or one above the maximum matching epic rank) and the first
matching insertion target's rank. `decideWithinCapacity`, which the writer actually calls, exposes every original
`decide` guarantee below capacity. History role standing specifies each of the five values; append, start and note
specify their contributor minimum.

`replayEvent` retains every `apply` postcondition while admitting a validated snapshot already at the maximum safe
cursor: every validated event is then stale and the snapshot is unchanged. `replayHistory` is the sequencer's actual
replay loop. It proves a safe monotone cursor, no more advances than input events, preservation of `0 <= rank < seq`,
and exact final numbering when events are contiguous from the initial snapshot. Schema decoding establishes its
preconditions. These clauses do not prove full replay-state equivalence, snapshot identity uniqueness, epic membership,
or journal ordering. The writer retains direct `apply`, whose precondition follows from an accepted capacity decision.

Two failing-first behavioral regressions found seed intent replay accepting an event past `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`.
It now uses the same capacity decision, preserving the final safe event and refusing subsequent intents. The complete
seed intent fold and refusal order still need contracts; malformed arbitrary starting snapshots are not claimed safe.
No dependency or compiler behavior changes.

The full positive gate passes all twelve modules: **5,588 isolated conversation batches plus 154 ordinary
obligations** in 336.462 seconds. All **451 current mutations** reject: 144 fresh history mutations in 383.912 seconds
and 307 byte-identical inherited inputs with matching manifests and actual Dafny failures. All current source hashes
still match after the roles and benchmark rebase. The inventory now contains **1,582 executable items**. Two new
seed regressions failed first; the focused history suite passes 26 tests. The nine history/seed benchmark workloads

## Eighth module batch: budget charge keys

A review between batches found that the API forwarded the bare reply id to the day's shared budget object. Every
conversation numbers its first reply `r1`, so two conversations' first replies collided under one `reply/r1` charge
key: the second conversation's spend read as a replay of the first and added nothing. The workerd regression runs
two conversations through the real reply flow against the real budget object and reads the ledger's charge keys
through the test host's new window: one merged key before the fix, two namespaced keys after. `chargeKeyOf` in
`budgetDecision` is proved to construct exactly `host + ":" + reply`; the API and the test host both forward
through it. The uniqueness theorem behind it is string concat-cancellation, which the backend's string reasoning
cannot prove even with length hints — recorded as `verify/bugs/string-concat-unique.ts` with its host reproduction,
not weakened. Three executable mutations (host dropped, separator dropped, arguments swapped) each fail the exact
construction contract.

its other twelve modules. The current **652/652** mutant copies match actual intended-function Dafny rejections:

## Thirteenth module batch: Post and StartTour continuations

The actual Post and StartTour bodies now thread begun/recorded/refused/dispatched state through their existing
journaled record and dispatch Actions. The shared kernel proves the reachable invariant: records are zero or one,

exact sum domain; no invalid settlement subtracts or poisons previously valid accounting. Invalidity latches through

**Viewport.** `src/web/viewport.vibe` held its follow state machine inline. It now keeps one `Viewport` value

- `pauseViewport`: an allowed upward gesture pauses, records the position and takes the next intent; a refused one
  changes nothing.
- `scrolledViewport`: an inactive page changes nothing; otherwise `bottom` is the exact resume rule, `paused` is its
  negation, a scroll off the bottom takes the next intent, and a repeated position-only pause on a hosted page reports
  nothing. Every step raises the intent by at most one, so from 0 the intent precondition holds for the first
  2^53−1 native events; beyond that is not proved.
- `followViewport`: only the newest intent on an active page with a newest entry scrolls, and only it resumes
  following.

  keys; Home or Command-Up go to the top, PageUp a page, ArrowUp a line. The PageUp distance (`Math.floor`) and the

- Response guards: a late outline is ignored once the page is ready; an accepted outline never lowers `latest` and
  is read again exactly when events arrived during its read (`outlineArrival`). A commit page applies only to the
  hash's commit and never replaces a newer read (`commitApplies`); matches apply only to the current filter.

  when none is under way (`eventArrival`).

  nothing; otherwise the epic's commits are replaced exactly from `from`, cut to `total`, at the first page of that
  epic, every other page unchanged. Pages with distinct epics stay distinct. The host replaced pages by object
  identity; the proof uses the first index, the same page under that invariant.
- Reads: page offsets 0, `PAGE`, … cover an epic's read commits, one page at least (`readOffsets`); a hash reads its
  commit, or its epic before that epic's first page (`hashRead`); opening an epic reads it only if unread; only a

## Witness statement (lane vl-proveall2, 2026-11-11)

**Gap.** `verify/bugs/forall-exists-witness.dfy`: Dafny 4.11 does not prove `forall i :: A ==> exists k :: B` from the
identical precondition. Z3 negates and skolemizes the goal to `i0`; `res[i0]` then occurs only under `k`'s binder, so
no ground term triggers the hypothesis. A Dafny forall statement that picks `k :| C` proves each instance but does not
close the postcondition either (tried on ints, strings and records; Boogie shows the two quantifiers differ only in
their skolems). Loops passed by chance, when an unrelated `parts[j]` happened to be ground.

**Fix (`packages/lemmascript`).** `//@ assert forall(i, A ==> exists(k, B)) by exists(k, C)` in a method. The emitter
names the body `A ==> exists k :: B` as a Dafny predicate over its free variables (parameters, locals, `\result`,
typed from the method); the method's requires and ensures clauses with the same body, up to their free variables,
use the same predicate, so a negated goal is the ground atom `!P(.., i0, ..)` and the forall statement's conclusion
matches it by congruence. A precondition whose `exists` part is the pick's is asserted at `i` before `var k :| C`.
Each named clause keeps its `X[i]` terms as alternative triggers, so callers instantiate it from their own terms.
Other methods emit exactly as before. Lean refuses the statement by name.

**Tests.** `forall-exists-witness.ts` proves a loop's per-piece origin and parity, the reproduction's `copy` from its
precondition, and a caller (7 obligations). Its `-red` twin is the same program without `by` and fails at both
postconditions; its `-wrong` twin flips the parity and fails the witness's own check. `forall-exists-witness.test.ts`:
splitting at a top-level `by` (not inside strings, parentheses or words), the emitted predicate, triggers and pick,
an unchanged contract without `by`, shape errors and the Lean refusal. Before the fix the fixture failed with
`Unexpected: by` and the test file failed to load.

**Proof.** `markdownDecision.inlinePieces` now also ensures every piece copies some part with that part's parity
(`\result[i].code == (k % 2 == 1)` for the `k` whose text it has). A new loop invariant carries it with `k < j`, and the
witness before `return` picks `k`. The loop's helper assertion now states the new piece's length and text but not
its parity, which the invariants carry: the old helper restated the body's parity, so it rejected every parity mutant
by itself, and under `md-inline-drop` Z3 sometimes reported its index-range error first, which is not a rejection.
The five `md-inline-*` mutants are rejected by an assertion or an invariant. No app mutant isolates the new clause:
flipping a repeated part's later copy (`(j % 2 === 1) !== (parts.indexOf(parts[j]!) < j)`) keeps every old clause true,
but Dafny cannot prove the coverage invariant for it, so it is not counted as evidence. The clause's strength is shown
by the LemmaScript `-wrong` twin, which has no coverage clause.

**Not proved.** The order of equal pieces. The statement covers one outer and one inner binder; nested binders and
functions (not methods) are refused with a message.

A broker state is the signed 43-character nonce; a pending start answers its own site and nonce before expiry; a Connect finishes only in the pressing session for the confirmed person, with a delegation and expiry; a direct callback needs the signed state and a code of at most 4096. Expiry, pruning, GitHub ids, self-grants, unchanged grants, the first-maintainer grant, the failure answer, the step outcome, the sandbox Origin rule, the admitted role and the account owner rule. |
| `worker/actionsDecision.vibe` | A declared body that is not digits or exceeds 32000 is refused; a cross-origin write is refused, a request without Origin is not; the collection routes and each run route; run ids are `a` and 1-64 of `[a-zA-Z0-9-]`; a write's status (accepted, 403 when forbidden, else 409 or 404); the actor (agent principal or agent door); a start under a used id with a different request conflicts; a Post's reply child is cancelled as its Post. |
| `worker/sandboxWorkerDecision.vibe` | A probe owner is `probe-` and 13 digits, admitted only while `now < deadline <= now + 600000`; a lease is at least 1000 ms and never beyond the deadline (1000 ms for an id with none); the probe principal and role; the probe routes (the sandbox protocol, and only POST for the sweep, the direct machine and the Container recording) and the two conversations a recording is read for; a Container recording erases every inactivity timeout and only the run script's fourth quoted word, and keeps a call at `stored + index` only below the limit; a container is running unless its machine answered `stopped`; a sandbox request reads, writes or is not found, and each write names what it lacks; 403 or 409; the gateway asks an account only for a signed-in starter; a read runs as the meter; only commands bypass the gate; a lease is live only when `running`. |
| `worker/draftDecision.vibe` | Usage settles as reported only with a call and no unreported call; a spent day is the budget's failure; a wiki draft is kept only for the page asked and with text; the agent drafts only a known page, never `decisions`. |
| `worker/workerDecision.vibe` | The site Worker's routes (the bound API, mock health, app pages, built assets) and its refusal of an asset answered with HTML; start-up and step outcomes, the retry after a failed start-up, the starting object's members (no `then`, no unknown name); a post's owner is written only with its Posted event; a VIP review's pull number is a positive decimal under the repository's pull prefix. |

**Obligations and mutations.** 133 Dafny obligations in five new modules (accounts 44, actions 25, sandbox 30,
drafts 4, worker 30). 127 new executable mutations in `verify/worker_mutations.py` (51, 19, 33,
7, 17), each rejected by Dafny. Five mutants first failed TypeScript or the RegExp subset and were rewritten as
type-correct edits; they are not counted twice. Red first: on main the five modules and their tests do not exist, so
every new unit test fails to load, and every mutant is a red run of its clause.

**Not proved, and why.** `ObjectStorage.eventKey` (that keys sort as events do): LemmaScript reads neither `String` of
a number nor `padStart` (`verify/bugs/event-key.ts`). `SandboxHttp`'s route captures use `exec`, refused by the RegExp
subset. `GitHubDelegate.asPerson` keeps its two Option tests in the shell, where TypeScript needs them to narrow, so a
proved copy would decide nothing. Native `trim`, `Number`, `Number.isSafeInteger`, JSON comparison, the newest-first
sort and the body reads' Option tags stay host boundaries, named per file in the inventory.

**Tool fixes (`packages/lemmascript`).** Three emitter defects found while proving these modules, each with a failing
test first:

1. `x === undefined || P(x)` did not narrow `x` on the right (`longEnough(text)` on an Option); `narrow.ts`
   `ruleOrOptional` now matches, nests one match per leading absence fact, and leaves a disjunction that never reads
   the value, or only compares it directly (`opt === null || x < opt`, already emitted), unchanged. `optional-or-narrowing.test.ts` was 1/3 before, 3/3 after; its fixture proves (3 obligations)
   and its `-wrong` twin fails.
2. Inside the arm that bound an optional, a presence check on it (`op !== undefined`) became `i_op_val != None`, a
   Dafny type error; `transform.ts` `presentPath` now makes it a constant.
3. `mapTStmt` dropped a loop's `decreases` and `doneWith`, so a narrowed measure kept the Option (`|text| - i`).
   `narrowed-presence.test.ts` was 1/3 before, 3/3 after; its fixture proves (2 obligations).

The RegExp matcher's 64-repeat limit is documented, not a defect: `resumeToken` is a proved loop instead.

**Inventory fix.** `functionBoundaries` was looked up only by the top-level function, so a nested key such as
`worker/Accounts.vibe:make/presented` never matched; the full label is now tried first (`inventory_test.cjs`).

## Proved lookups and gates behind three classified rows (lane vl-proveall2, 2026-11-12)

**Scope.** The lead gave this lane the 34 open rows in `src/actions/agent.vibe`, `tools.vibe`, `catalog.vibe`,
`src/core/issueFlows.vibe`, `wikiFlows.vibe`, `issueSchemas.vibe`, `accountCookies.vibe`,
`src/history/MythicalHistory.vibe` and `src/surfaces/manifest.vibe`, and `record-journal-order`. vl-proveall3 landed
reasons for the same rows (third-lane batches 33 to 35) and the journal-order assertion first, so this batch keeps
their entries and proves the three decisions they describe as unchecked claims:

| Decision | What the proof states |
| --- | --- |
| `catalogDecision.entryAllowed` | Over the shared `mayRun`: an internal entry is never run; a viewer's entry, by anyone; a maintainer's, by a maintainer; any other least role, by a contributor or a maintainer. The catalog's `allowed`, which every action door calls (MockActions, ActionsHttp, ActionRuns, ActionDirectory), is this decision. |
| `accountCookieDecision.sessionCookieOf` | An origin starting `https:` uses the host-prefixed session cookie; any other, the plain one. `accountCookies.sessionCookieName` is this function. |
| `flowPolicyDecision.issueOperations`, `wikiOperations`, `issueOperationIndex`, `wikiOperationIndex` | Every issue operation (13) and wiki operation (4) is in its list (each list's own postcondition, so dropping one fails the list), at an index in range that holds it. `issueFlow` and `wikiEditFlow` index the flows they build from those lists, so their `!` never fails. Before, the inventory said the `find` had exactly one match, but TypeScript did not check that the hand-written lists covered the operation types. |

**Tool fix (`packages/lemmascript`).** Stating each list's completeness needed `\result.includes("read")` on a
`ReadonlyArray<IssueOperation>`. LemmaScript emitted the literal as a Dafny `string` searched for in `seq<Op>`, a type
error, though TypeScript reads it as the union member. A value searched for with `includes` or `indexOf` now takes
the array's element type, as `push` and `with` already did. Red first: `union-search.test.ts` 1/2 and the fixture
failed with the same type errors; after, 2/2, the fixture proves (4 obligations) and its `-wrong` twin, a list that
lacks a member it claims, fails. A typed quantifier (`forall(op: IssueOperation, \result.includes(op))`) does not
prove: Dafny does not split the enum under the binder. Arrays' `lastIndexOf` is still unsupported by the emitter.

**Stale and uncountable mutations.** `d1c7cc2f` nested `newCommitOrder`'s unreached-cursor test under
`cursor !== ""`, so `main-order-unreached` (`extended_mutations.py`) matched nothing and the full `verify:broken`
stopped before any mutant ran. It now makes the nested branch answer `[]` and fails its own postcondition; the old edit
(`at < -1`) would read `fetched[-1]` first, an index error rather than a contract failure. `history-merge-detached`
(`web_mutations.py`) timed out in the whole `mergedPages_ensures` lemma at 30 s and at 120 s, with or without this
batch's LemmaScript change; it is now checked against the one clause it breaks (a detached page changes nothing,
`mutation_targets.POSTCONDITIONS`) and rejected there. `mutations.py --check` names every case whose text no longer
matches exactly once and writes no mutant; `harness_test.py` runs it (about a second), so `pnpm verify` reports a stale
case. It failed on the stale `screen-sandbox-request` (since fixed on main by vl-proveall3) and passes on every case.


**Obligations and mutations.** catalogDecision 4, accountCookieDecision 8 and flowPolicyDecision 11 Dafny obligations,
every one verified. Nine new mutations in `verify/worker_mutations.py` (3 entryAllowed, 2 sessionCookieOf, 4 operation
lists and indexes), each rejected. Red first: on main the new functions do not exist, so the new tests in
`test/flowPolicyDecision.test.vibe` and `test/chunkCookieCatalog.test.vibe` fail to load, and each mutant is a red run
of its clause.

## Product defects

**Saved theatre audio shape.** An injected Window service returning JSON `null` breaks speech control; wrong-type
Boolean fields can incorrectly suppress a new utterance. Validate StoredAudio before its fields reach the proved
policy. Three strengthened regressions fail before validation, and all sixteen pass afterward.

- **Two conversations shared one budget charge.** The daily ledger dedupes by reply id, and every conversation's
  first reply is `r1`; the API forwarded it bare, so a second conversation's first reply was never charged. Found
  between batches by reviewing the wiring the proofs call; the regression failed before the namespaced key fix.

- **Seed replay could overflow a valid cursor.** Starting at the safe maximum, or reaching it on one intent and then
  replaying another, produced cursor `9007199254740992`. Both regressions failed before the capacity decision was
  applied to seed replay.

- **Conversation storage bypassed its numeric and event-shape proof domain.** A faulty Log could supply negative,
  fractional or unsafe cursors, malformed text or unknown variants before replay. EventSchema decoding now rejects
  these rows with no write/dispatch and no stored content in diagnostics. The regression failed before the fix.


- **Unsafe history ranks broke distinct insertion positions.** Plain numeric schemas admitted negative, fractional,
  nonfinite and unsafe integer ranks. Safe integer plus `rank < seq` validation now protects every replay/bootstrap
  boundary, and the proved writer refuses capacity exhaustion. The final safe event is stored once; the next intent
  is refused without writes. Four regression tests failed before the fix; all six boundary tests now pass.
- **Cached history follow bypassed validation; snapshot errors exposed stored content.** A later store read could
  stream an invalid event, and HistoryObject's early JSON decode could reveal stored text in diagnostics. Follow
  validates each reread; stored JSON uses a redacted decoder. Both new regressions failed before the fixes.

- **Unsafe usage and corrupt totals bypassed accounting's proof domain.** Overflow could replace a valid daily sum
  with an inexact value; a negative total could be charged or admitted. Admission and spend now check persisted
  safe integers and a proved sum guard. Overflow and invalid totals fail without writes; exact maximum charging and
  repeated oversized telemetry are covered by regressions.

- **Non-finite usage poisoned the daily ledger.** A provider's NaN or Infinity made the total unusable. The regression
  `budgetProof.test.vibe` failed first with NaN instead of 13. Non-finite usage now adds zero; finite negative usage
  still clamps to zero and finite usage retains its rounding. Existing spends, the storage lock, logging and metrics remain.

- **The proof harness could check zero sources.** A prospective source nested under `.checks` was ignored by the
  directory scanner, so it said “0 files checked” and exited zero. `verify/harness_test.py` reproduces that failure
  first. The harness now supplies every staged source explicitly, rejects an empty selection, and runs its regression
  tests before every proof invocation. Production and mutation receipts preceding this fix checked 4 and 84 sources;
  the prospective receipts with zero checked sources are superseded, not counted as validation.

- **Lifecycle tests assumed Web Crypto had finished after 200 yields.** The baseline flow reproduced the failure.
  The concurrency and disposal tests now await real ReplyFinished/ReplyDelta events and retain their assertions,
  including live follower and worker shutdown. The repaired lifecycle suite passes 9/9 and the full suite 177/177.
- **Discovery and inventory could omit source.** Whitespace-aware marker discovery now has a regression. The
  inventory used UTF-16 positions against byte-based projection mappings; it now reads original-source ESTree,
  includes methods/effect blocks, rejects parse failures, and passes four source-enumeration regressions.

- **The startup browser check assumed health always beat its deadline.** The faulty transport now observes
  cancellation. Review rejected accepting either timeout or settlement, which could hide blocked keyboard handling.
  The browser host injects a Clock that holds the health deadline, while forwarding real time reads and other sleeps;
  startup passes its Clock service to the backend resource layer. Keyboard/post assertions deliberately run beyond
  the ordinary deadline and require health to remain uncancelled, then settle on release. The regression failed first;
  all 12 startup browser cases pass. Independent backend TestClock cases still require the exact three-second timeout.
  The 6,737-commit bootstrap integration exceeded the default five-second unit budget under shared host load; its
  integration budget is 20 seconds, with all replay equality, uniqueness and count assertions unchanged.

- **The announcement browser test could miss all partial renders.** Under shared host load, rendering coalesced the
  real deltas and terminal event before the browser observed a nonempty unfinished answer. The transport fault now
  holds each real ReplyFinished until the test observes the nonempty streaming text and unchanged announcement,
  then releases it. It preserves all event contents, order, accessibility checks and complete-answer assertions.

- **The sandbox alarm test assumed a fixed number of scheduler yields completed native asynchronous work.**
  The inherited test failed with no later meter event after startup. Its logger now signals an observer installed
  only after startup completes; the test awaits a real later alarm event and retains the idle/count-increase/stopped
  assertions. Review caught that an earlier observer could be satisfied by startup's own meter log; that preliminary
  receipt is superseded. The corrected focused test passes.

Two additional probes strictly typecheck but do not verify:

- `unicode-case.ts` / `~/vl/vibelang-bugs/lemmascript-unicode-case/`: JavaScript maps `K` (U+212A) to `k`. LemmaScript
  now models `toLowerCase` and `toUpperCase` as exact only on ASCII strings and unknown elsewhere (third-lane case
  mapping fix), so this correct contract still cannot be proved, and no false one can. Unicode normalization in
  keyboard shortcuts and mock selection remains a runtime boundary; normalized-input policies can still be proved.
- `event-key.ts` / `~/vl/vibelang-bugs/lemmascript-event-key/`: production `String(seq).padStart(16, "0")`
  fails emission. The fixed-width key contract is retained; storage-key lexical ordering is not proved.

- `filter-method.ts` / `~/vl/vibelang-bugs/lemmascript-filter-method/`: a single-expression Array.filter callback
  calling a verified loop-backed predicate fails as an unsupported multi-statement Dafny lambda. The unanswered-post
  selector's complete production contract is retained in its prospective proof; no selection proof is yet claimed.

- `empty-string-union.ts` / `~/vl/vibelang-bugs/lemmascript-empty-string-union/`: an empty-string alternative in a
  string-literal union becomes an empty Dafny constructor (`Route.`), which the backend cannot parse. The typed route
  reproduction retains both exact outcomes; no production contract is suppressed.

- `union-widening.ts` / `~/vl/vibelang-bugs/lemmascript-union-widening/`: a narrow string union returned as its
  wider union strictly typechecks, but the backend emits incompatible Dafny datatypes. The pending overlay-priority
  extraction exposed this gap. Its exact-value reproduction is retained; the existing UI remains intact, with no
  production workaround or weakened contract.

- `real-rounding.ts` / `~/vl/vibelang-bugs/lemmascript-real-rounding/`: an exact-real arithmetic theorem passes,
  while native execution of the same function violates it at `(100, 50, 1.9999999999999998)`. The native assertion
  intentionally fails. This records the IEEE-754 boundary; neither result is counted as a rejected mutation.

Each new fixture also lives at `~/vl/vibelang-bugs/lemmascript-<name>/` with its command. These are not mutation
successes. Compiler/runtime execution of Effect, Schema and Foldkit remains outside LemmaScript's plain subset.

The resumed codec/Markdown probes retain `json-roundtrip.ts` (all message fields), `uri-roundtrip.ts` (printable
ASCII, excluding native malformed-surrogate exceptions), and the exact production `markdown-safe-link.ts` scheme
filter. All strictly typecheck; JSON.stringify and regex literals fail emission, and URI codecs are unresolved in
Dafny. These refine the existing codec/regexp gaps; none is counted as a proof or rejected mutation. Reproductions
are `~/vl/vibelang-bugs/lemmascript-<fixture-name>/`.

The history tool request prototype additionally exposes `optional-union-default.ts`, reproduced at
`~/vl/vibelang-bugs/lemmascript-optional-union-default/`: a strictly typed two-variant output with a defaulted
optional input emits incompatible bare-string/Option branches and a match on `seq<char>`. Dafny reports two
resolution/type errors, not a contract failure. The production `requestOf` remains unchanged and unproved; the
exact reproduction contract is retained.

`safe-usage-integer.ts` / `~/vl/vibelang-bugs/lemmascript-safe-usage-integer/` strictly typechecks, but native
`Number.isSafeInteger` fails Dafny emission as an unsupported method call. The exact range contract is retained.
The Reply integer kernel proves its admission policy over the supplied native observations; malformed-number
regressions exercise the actual observation calls. This is a tool failure and never a rejected mutation.

### Twentieth batch: walkthrough counters and scalar controls

The actual walk uses `nextTourCounter` for private visit/hold identities. Its native-number predecessor fails the
regression after `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (unreachable in practice: about 9 quadrillion steps in one tour): the next two values both become 9007199254740992, repeating durable
step names. Private counters now use BigInt, with an exact-plus-one contract, strict progress and nonnegative closure.
They never enter journal payloads; step names remain decimal strings and match every previously exact counter value.
`firstTourVisit` proves zero-only saved-state admission; `tourWait` proves pause waits for control without starting a
reading clock; `tourControlChoice` proves exact seek versus retained current step; `nextTourStep` proves one bounded
clock advance. The actual clock cursor is bounded by the finite walkthrough script. Existing Actions, log/span/count
steps and cancellation are retained. No new dependency, UI copy or compiler behavior changes.

The seven counter regressions and 33 flow-module proof units pass. All 141 current module mutants (12 new) reject, and
the full proof gate passes 17/17 modules. The full optional restored-cursor composition remains unproved because the exact minimal
nullable-record guard/union contracts still fail backend resolution; those contracts are retained unchanged. BigInt
itself compiles and verifies successfully and is not a tool gap. Whole-app proof coverage remains incomplete.

### Twenty-first batch: web update guards

`src/web/modelDecision.vibe` holds 19 decisions that `update` in `src/web/main.vibe` previously wrote inline; every
call site now runs the proved function, with no behavior change. Stale-response fences cover actions epochs (an absent
epoch reads as zero), issue retries and details, and wiki requests. `slashHighlight` stays inside the menu after the
menu shrinks. 23 proof units; 49 new mutations reject. `update` itself remains unproved: LemmaScript cannot read the
Foldkit message match or the Model spreads, so the frame of each arm is covered by tests.

## LemmaScript is a workspace package

`packages/lemmascript` (`@smthrs/lemmascript`) is a copy of LemmaScript 0.6.6 (midspiral/lemmascript, tag `v0.6.6`, commit
`736fb7ce5ef89555b566bdbcca0c8fe057fbb205`, MIT). `verify/install.sh` builds it and links `verify/.tools/bin/lsc` to it;
npm no longer supplies the tool. Its 317 upstream unit tests and its Dafny fixtures pass in the package's `test` target.

Local patches, listed in the package README and offered upstream later (Will decides any GitHub contribution):

| Patch | Test |
| --- | --- |
| Object spread of a conditional over two object literals | `tools/fixtures/object-spread-conditional.ts` |
| Object spread of a value holding a strict subset of the base record's fields | `tools/fixtures/object-spread-partial.ts` |
| An exhaustive `X.match(value, { Tag: arm })` table over a `_tag` union, in return position, read as a `switch` | `tools/fixtures/tagged-match.ts`, `tagged-match-wrong-arm.ts`, `tagged-match-missing-arm.ts` |

The previous note that 0.6.6 could not read Model spreads was too broad: plain and nested record spreads already proved.
The two spread forms above were the gaps.

VL-5: `ts-morph` 25.0.1 was already this toolchain's dependency through the npm package; it now appears in the pnpm lockfile
with `tsx`, `typescript` and `@types/node` at monorepo versions. `lemmascript-claimcheck` is dropped: `lsc claimcheck` reports it missing.

### Next tool gap for `update`

`update` is still unproved. Under ts-morph the real Foldkit `Message` has members typed `{ [x: string]: any }` where a payload
uses `Schema.*`, because LemmaScript's checker does not see the VibeLang compiler's types, and `schema` declarations are not
TypeScript. The tagged-match reader needs a literal `_tag` on every member, so it declines the real table.
Reproduction: `~/vl/vibelang-bugs/lemmascript-vibe-typed-message` on nyc-01.
Fixed in the thirty-second batch: a proof module names the real `Message` through `import type` and main.vibe's emitted
declaration. The table in `main.vibe` itself is still unproved; see that batch.

### Twenty-second batch: account arms of `update` on plain types

Route chosen by the lead (2026-11-09): `update`'s arms move, batch by batch, onto plain declared state with commands as a
data union that `main.vibe` interprets. 14 account arms (`ClickedAccount`, `ClickedSignIn`, `ClickedSignOut`, `ClickedPeople`,
`ClosedPeople`, `ToggledPeople`, `SelectedRole`, `CancelledRole`, `ConfirmedRole`, `GrantedRole`, `FailedRoles`, `AccountFailed`,
`DismissedAccountError`, `RetriedAccount`) now call one proved function each in `src/web/modelDecision.vibe`, over
`AccountScreen` and `AccountCommand`. Each contract states the exact next state, frame included, and the exact command list
with its order. 39 new mutations reject. Every app test passes unchanged.

Boundaries that remain: the Foldkit message table selects the arm (`Message.match` in `main.vibe`), `runAccount` and
`accountCommand` translate the plain result, and `SelectedRole`'s `canSelectRole` guard and `RetriedAccount`'s sign-in branch stay in
`update`, so that a refused role returns the same model object and a retried sign-in passes through `update`'s post-processing as
before. `update` as a whole is not yet proved: the arms not listed above are still inline.

LemmaScript's contract parser gained the record spread its IR already had (`\result.state == { ...state, f: v }`), and a contract
literal on the right of `==` takes the left operand's declared type. Fixtures: `tools/fixtures/spec-record-spread.ts` and
`spec-record-spread-wrong.ts`; units: `tools/tests/spec-record-spread.test.ts`.

`ClickedActions`, `MaximizedActions`, `SelectedAction`, `UpdatedActionInput`, `RetriedActions` and `FailedActions` call proved functions over
`ActionScreen` and `ActionCommand`, with exact next state and command lists; 16 mutations reject. `FailedActions` keeps its proved

`SelectedRun` (they carry schema arrays), `SelectedActionStep` and `TickedActions` (one optional field each, `ActionView.step` and `.now`), and `MovedSlash` (one proved call).

### Twenty-fourth batch: sandbox and wiki-editor arms of `update`

`src/web/paneDecision.vibe` proves `StartedSandbox`, `StoppedSandbox`, `SubmittedTerminal` (through `startSandboxAction`), `LoadedSandbox`, `FailedSandbox`, `UpdatedWikiEdit`, `SubmittedWikiEdit`, `BeganWikiEdit` and `FailedWikiEdit`, with exact next state and command lists over plain types; 49 mutations reject. `sandboxNotice` proves which minute notice shows; `main.vibe` renders the text. Not proved: the operation id `${session}/sandbox/${request}` (number-to-string formatting), and the arms that set one field or call one proved function (`ClickedSandboxes`, `MaximizedSandboxes`, `UpdatedTerminal`, `CanceledWikiEdit`). `CompletedWikiEdit` stays inline: it filters the observed page list. `wikiEditError` moved into the proved module.

Tool gaps: `lsc` emitted an invalid Dafny constructor for `""` in a string-literal union, fixed in `packages/lemmascript` with fixtures `empty-string-union.ts` and `empty-string-union-wrong.ts`. ### Twenty-fifth batch: `decide` is its own proof module

`decide` and `apply` were 95% of `conversation.vibe`'s assertion batches (`decide` 8,865, `apply` 9,751 of 19,918; 3,492 solver-seconds in total; no batch over 8 s), so moving lemmas out could not shorten the run. `decide`, `accepted`, `refused`, `Intent`, `Decision`, `Refusal` and `MAX_TEXT` moved to `src/core/decide.vibe`; `MAX_TEXT` moved because nothing else reads it and an imported constant is an `lsc` gap (`~/vl/vibelang-bugs/lemmascript-imported-const`). No contract changed. All 33 `decide` clauses are textually identical (with `res` written as the call), `decide_ensures` has no `assume`, and all 85 mutations of `decide`, `accepted` and `refused` reject.

`decide` now proves against the verified contracts of the imported `canGrant`, `canReplyTo`, `hasClientId`, `hasEntryId`, `isReplying`, `isTouring`, `may`, `roleOf` and `runOpen`, emitted as `{:axiom}` with their source contracts; `conversation.vibe` proves those. `check.py` stages an imported `./x.vibe` as `x.vibe.ts` so `lsc` reads its contracts. Because `decide` now calls only contracts, `lsc` emits a function plus `decide_ensures` instead of a method; `postcondition_line` looks at the lemma first. Result: `decide.vibe` 509 assertion batches in 33 s against 8,865, and the module is no longer the wall-time risk.

### Twenty-sixth batch: issue arms of `update`

`src/web/issueDecision.vibe` (20 Dafny items) proves `issueAction`, every branch of the issues screen: the role gates, the single saved retry (a saved action blocks another durable action; reads and drafts are not saved), the wizard's bounds (`step` stays in 1..4), the first missing field of each step, and that a refused action returns the same state. It also proves `issueUiEffects`, `openedIssueCard`, `clickedIssuesLoads`, `issueProjectionApplies`, `issueDataApplies`, `issueDefaultRole`, `issueAssigneeAfter`, `issueRecovered` and `issueRecoveredView`, `issueLoaded`, `issueFailed`, `issueFailureText` and `issueDetailsFailed`. `issuesUpdate` and the arms `OpenIssueCard`, `IssueProjectionLoaded`, `ClickedIssues`, `IssueUi`, `IssuesLoaded`, `IssuesFailed`, `IssueDetailsLoaded` and `IssueDetailsFailed` are shells over them. 102 mutations, all rejected. Not proved, read by the shells as facts: `trim`, `Number` and the array searches for the assignee and the newest issue; building the request (`issueRequest`); the `reason === "connect"` choice in `IssuesFailed`, left in the shell because decision 0165 replaces that path.

Tool gap fixed: `lsc` rewrote a string-literal union member spelled `none` to Option's `None` and emitted an unresolved constructor, in `packages/lemmascript` with fixtures `none-string-union.ts` and `none-string-union-wrong.ts`.

### Twenty-seventh batch: tour control and stream arms of `update`

`src/web/tourDecision.vibe` (14 Dafny items) proves the tour controls (no tour means no command; back stops at the first stop), the sound toggle, the late end, which failed start keeps control, the conditions for the automatic tour, the failed and reopened event stream (a reconnect takes a new epoch and resumes from the last applied event), and the slash menu opened by the draft. `ClickedPauseTour`, `ClickedBackStop`, `ClickedSkipStop`, `ToggledTourSound`, `RemeasureTheatre`, `SucceededTour`, `FailedTour`, `AutoTour`, `FailedEvents`, `ClickedReconnect` and `UpdatedDraft` are shells over them. 27 mutations, all rejected.

48 of the 100 arms now call proved functions. Still inline: the remaining 52 arms; the `Message.match` table; `runAccount`, `accountCommand`, `runActions`, `actionCommand`, `runTourControl`, `issueScreen`, `issueFacts`; `update`'s post-processing.

`verify:broken --module <file>` runs only one module's mutations, for iterating. A landing runs the whole suite.

### Twenty-eighth batch: Escape, tour receive, account events, applied events, post-processing

`src/web/updateDecision.vibe` proves Escape's ladder (the tour is taken back first; otherwise exactly one thing closes, innermost first; a submitting wiki editor stays), the plan for an applied conversation event (a gap replays and applies nothing; only an advancing `PaneOpened` moves panes; only an advancing `ActionRequested` reads an action), `update`'s post-processing (a changed person or role re-gates the issue dialog; a running tour remeasures except after a measurement or focus return). `tourDecision.vibe` adds Learn more, ending a tour, the tour event receipt (a dismissed tour presents nothing) and the table of stops. `modelDecision.vibe` adds `AccountLoaded` and `ReceivedRole` (a grant changes my role only when it is mine; a changed account retires what was scoped to the old one). `PressedEscape`, `ReceivedTourEvent`, `ClickedLearnMore`, `ClickedEndTour`, `AccountLoaded`, `ReceivedRole`, `ReceivedEvent` are shells over them. 141 mutations, all rejected.

Tool boundary: a string-literal union is a separate Dafny datatype and does not pass to a `string` parameter (`~/vl/vibelang-bugs/lemmascript-union-to-string`). `roleDialogCloses` now takes the role union its callers already pass; its contract is unchanged.

### Twenty-ninth batch: submit, launch, run selection, issue request fields

`updateDecision.vibe` proves what a submitted draft becomes, the tour's demonstration post (not counted in the tab's numbering), which commands switch the mode, and when a run starts or retries. `modelDecision.vibe` proves run selection. `issueDecision.vibe` proves the request text and the parent number. `submit`, `launchAction`, `switchMode`, `SelectedRun`, `StartedAction`, `parentNumber` and `issueRequest` call them. 36 mutations, all rejected.

60 of the 100 arms now call proved functions. Still inline: the remaining 40 arms, of which many return the model or issue one fixed command; the `Message.match` table, which the tool cannot read (`lemmascript-vibe-typed-message`); the translation helpers `runEscape`, `runAccount`, `accountCommand`, `runActions`, `actionCommand`, `runTourControl`, `issueScreen`, `issueFacts`; `mergeRuns` in `actionModel.vibe`, which is outside this lane; the issue operation key format.
## Third proofs lane (vl-proveall3): history, core, surfaces and worker logic

This lane proves the pure parts of the sequencers, the commands and the worker outside `src/web`. Its batches are
numbered on their own, so they never collide with the other two lanes' numbers.

### Third-lane batch 1: sequencer and command decisions

Four modules, each proved by `pnpm verify` and mutated by `pnpm verify:broken`:

| Module | What its contracts state | Called from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/history/stackDecision.vibe` | A plan's step: an amend is never title-checked; an empty title is refused before a long one; an admitted insert inserts; an admitted append opens its new epic first, else appends. `pairCut` moves a cut back one unit exactly when it would split a surrogate pair. `foldTitle` keeps a title that fits and otherwise cuts it there and adds "…", within the limit. `epicByTitle` is the first epic with that title, or `""` when none has it. | `src/history/Sequencer.vibe` (`plan`, `fold`), `src/history/seed.vibe` (`clip`) |
| `src/core/followDecision.vibe` | The replay cut is the later of the follower's cursor and the last number replayed; an event goes on exactly when it is above the cut. | both sequencers' `follow` |
| `src/core/sequencerDecision.vibe` | `attemptOf` is one more than the reply's restarts, counted by a recursive prefix measure. `restartCount` is the attempts skipped, never negative. `entryIndex` is the first match or -1. `finishPlan` keeps what streamed when the model text starts with it, else restarts; in both cases what is kept plus what is appended is exactly the model text. `settleStep` records only while the reply streams and repeats as `done` only when it already settled the same way. `spoken` and `tourSettles` choose the tour's paragraph break and its end. | `worker/Sequencer.vibe` |
| `src/surfaces/commandDecision.vibe` (12 new functions) | CLI and MCP argument validation: `--amend` before `--before` before append, and the commit each names; `history` reads an epic page or else a search, never both, and refuses only an unknown `--epic`; a page totals by its epic; `issue` details the specification for `spec-` operations and a bare `read`; a resume needs operation and key, its recovery rides only with it; a forbidden write says so; `wiki read` defaults to the index; `run --wait` fails unless a settled run passed; an action failure names its code. | `src/surfaces/commands.vibe` |

How the follow proof composes: each sequencer subscribes before it reads, so a live event is either in the replay or
after it. The replay is the stored events above the cursor, in order; the live filter passes only events above the cut.
The proved cut and freshness make an event at or below the replay's end arrive once. Ordering and completeness of the
store, PubSub delivery and locking are runtime behavior, not proved here.

a commit of main whose title had an emoji at units 198 and 199 folded into a title ending in a lone `\uD83D`, and
`encodeURIComponent` throws on it. The seed's `clip` had the same cut. Both now call `pairCut`. Regressions:
`test/stackDecision.test.vibe` ("never splits a character when the sequencer folds a commit of main", "when the seed
clips a commit's title"), failing before the fix.

Dafny reserves with a trailing `_` (`fresh` becomes `fresh_`). `verify/sources.py` now has `dafny_name`, reading the
keyword set from `packages/lemmascript/tools/src/dafny-emit.ts`, used by the emission check, the diagnostic mapping
and `mutation_targets.py`. Regression: `harness_test.py`
`test_a_function_named_by_a_dafny_keyword_is_verified_under_its_escaped_name`, failing before the fix.

`restartsBefore_ensures` gets its checked induction step from `proof_additions.py`, as `runningCountPrefix` does.

`seed.vibe` builds a mythical history from main's commits and the merge queue. Its regular expressions, Maps and the commit graph walk stay outside LemmaScript; the choices they feed now live in `src/history/seedDecision.vibe`, and `seed.vibe` calls them.

| `entryUse` | Regenerated docs and open entries count for nothing; `landed` is claimed; `rejected`, `superseded` and `withdrawn` are attempts. | `seedOf` |
| `joins` | Exact precedence: regenerated docs join the commit before them only when there is one; then a revert joins what it reverts; then a landed entry's later commits join its first; else a new commit. | `seedOf` |
| `lastFitEnd` | Defined recursively: the last of the first `end` sentence ends that is at most `max`, else -1; never above `max`. | `sentenceCut` |
| `sentenceCut` | With every end at least 1: after the last sentence that fits; else after the first sentence when it is within the note limit; else -1 (the note is dropped, never cut mid-sentence). | `wholeSentences` |
| `evidenceStep` | A trailer starts a paragraph; a nonblank line that starts nothing of its own wraps; anything else closes. A wrap needs an open paragraph, so `paragraphs[length - 1]` exists. | `evidenceOf` |
| `foldedTitle` | A fold's stored title, or the mythical commit's own when the seed stored it empty. | `intentsOf` |

### Third-lane batch 5: when the next sandbox meter is due

`sandboxDecision.vibe` proves `meterDelay`, which `meterDelayMilliseconds` in `sandboxMeter.vibe` now calls with the one-minute interval. Its contract: the delay is at least 1 ms and at most the interval; below the interval it is at least `remaining / share` and one less is below it, where `share` is the running count or 1 when none runs. So the next meter falls on the first whole millisecond at which running × elapsed reaches the remaining allowance, and a running sandbox never goes a whole interval unmetered.

The contract states the bound as a quotient, not as `\result * share >= remaining`. The two are equivalent for `share >= 1`, but Dafny's default solver settings leave nonlinear arithmetic off, and the gate keeps one setting for every module. Mutations: 4.

### Third-lane batch 6: the issues host's decisions

`worker/Issues.vibe` answers every issues request against GitHub. Its choices now live in `src/core/issueHostDecision.vibe`; `Issues.vibe` calls them, and `Wiki.vibe` calls `requestKey`.

| Function | What its contract states | Called from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `keyUnit`, `requestKey` | A key is 1 to 100 units, each an ASCII letter, digit or `-`: exactly `/^[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,100}$/`, which every call replaces. | `serveIssues`, `executeIssues`, `serveWiki`, `executeWiki` |
| `failureReason`, `carriesCode` | Exact precedence: an outcome GitHub may have applied is `unknown`, then `partial`, then `rate-limited`, then 401, 403 and 404, else `unavailable`. Only `unknown`, `rate-limited` and `unavailable` carry a retry code. | `issueFailureOf` |
| `badRequest`, `refusalStatus` | Each refusal's HTTP status; every status is one of 400, 401, 403, 404, 409 and 503. | `serveIssues` |
| `checkedBeforeWrite`, `unwritten` | A failure is `unwritten` exactly when its execution is the first, nothing was written, and a check every write waits for refused it; a touched request never is. | `githubHost` |
| `agentRefused` | A device sign-in is refused accept and decline, and only those. | `githubHost`, `executeIssues` |
| `issueTask`, `vipState` | A task needs the task label and an assignee, then closed is Done, running is Running, else Queued. Only a verified marker makes a VIP; Accepted wins over Declined. | `githubHost` read |
| `projectedVip` | An Accepted label without this project's receipt is stored as In review; the result is Accepted only with a receipt; other states are kept. | `executeIssues` |
| `revisionRoom`, `validRevision`, `nextRevision` | The stored revision has room; observations are in range; the result advances past storage, reaches GitHub’s revision, and stays safe when its admitted inputs do. | `executeIssues` |
| `resumable`, `resumeStatus` | A read resumes exactly the durable writes, never `read` or `draft`; a resumed run is completed, failed, or running until it settles. | `executeIssues` |
| `choiceLabel`, `choiceLogin` | The configured agent is offered as `VibeLang agent`, and that label reads back as the agent; any other login reads back as itself. | `githubHost` |
| `timelineText` | The exact sentence for labeled, unlabeled, assigned, unassigned, closed and reopened events; `""` for a label or assignment event without its object, and for every other event. | `githubHost` read |

The refactor keeps behavior: the issues and wiki suites pass unchanged, and `test/issueHostDecision.test.vibe` compares `requestKey` with the old pattern on edge keys and pins each decision and `issueFailureOf`.

Tool gap found and fixed: LemmaScript's Dafny keyword set lacked `assigned`, `hide` and `ORDINAL`, so a parameter named `assigned` emitted Dafny that does not parse. Each was checked against Dafny 4.11's parser; the fix is in `packages/lemmascript/tools/src/dafny-emit.ts`, with a regression in `tools/tests/dafny-emit.test.ts`. A sweep of Dafny 4's reserved words found no other gap.

Not proved: the delegation refusal branch of `issueFailureOf` and every Connect GitHub step (smithers.sh decision 0165), GitHub paging and decoding, the VIP marker regexp, the parent URL parse, assignee order and case-insensitive matching, write order, and the engine, inspection and storage steps of `executeIssues`. `Accounts.vibe`'s `/api/auth/connect` resume check keeps its own pattern and list; it is on the Connect GitHub path.

Mutations: 37 in `issueHostDecision.vibe`.

Native applicability: `revisionRoom` refuses a negative or exhausted stored integer; `validRevision` admits only
nonnegative safe observed integers. The Worker also requires native `Number.isSafeInteger` before either decision.
Corrupt/fractional stored revisions and exhaustion previously reached the host and overwrote state; four regression
cases failed before these guards. A valid maximum-minus-one revision advances once to the maximum, and the next
observation refuses before host work without rewriting it. Faulty-host revision regressions pin the observation gate.
The native predicate itself remains the documented `safe-usage-integer.ts` boundary.

### Third-lane tool fix: case mapping

LemmaScript modelled `toLowerCase` and `toUpperCase` by mapping ASCII letters and keeping every other code unit, with
`|result| == |s|`. JavaScript applies Unicode's full case mappings, so the model proved false claims:
`String.fromCharCode(931).toLowerCase()` stays U+03A3 (JavaScript gives U+03C3), and `toUpperCase` keeps every
length (JavaScript uppers `ß` to `SS`). Both claims verified before the fix. No app proof used either method, so no
landed claim was wrong.

The fix in `packages/lemmascript/tools/src/dafny-emit.ts` makes each an axiom exact on ASCII strings, where JavaScript
maps A-Z or a-z unit for unit, and silent on any other string. Fixtures: `string-case.ts` proves the ASCII facts;
`string-case-wrong.ts` and `string-case-length-wrong.ts` must fail on a proof obligation (`tools/test-fixtures.sh`).

## Portable gate tooling (vl-gatefix, 2026-11-10)

The inventory now discovers `//@ verify` per function rather than requiring a manually maintained module note.
This fixes the stale “Not yet proved” rows for `decide` and other already marked functions; custom notes still state
the scope of their contracts. `verify/lsc_fresh.py` repairs copied or absolute lsc links to a relative workspace link
before compilation, so a packed tree uses the vendored LemmaScript and resolves its own dependencies.
Assertion-isolated positive proofs now use at most two Dafny cores, matching the lane rule and 4-vCPU box budget.

## Strengthening lane (vl-proof-strengthen, 2026-11-10)

The proof review (lane vl-review-proofs) found proved contracts too weak to catch real bugs: Dafny accepted four
mutants that broke authorization, action runs and the money paths. The changes below add contracts,
product fixes and honest labels, with the review's mutant (or the closest executable one) added to `mutations.py` and
rejected.

| Finding | Before | Now | Mutants added, all rejected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Self-grant | `decide` proved only `id != ""`, `role != "viewer"` and the other-person maintainer case | `decide`'s `GrantRole` result equals `canGrant(...)`, refused `forbidden`, and the event copies every field; `canGrant` proves a person's own grant only lowers their current (first-grant) role, with `roleOf`'s new first-grant witness | `decide-self-grant`, `decide-grant-event`, `cangrant-self-current` |
| 2. Authorization | Pinned only `merge`, `settings`, `roles` | `Authorize` result equals `may(roleOf(roles, by), action)` for every action, refused `forbidden`; `may` and `roleOf` are exact, so the HTTP gates are closed end to end | `decide-authorize-narrow` |
| 3. Budget bound (product bug) | `admit` read the ledger outside the lock and reserved nothing: twenty concurrent admissions at limit − 1 all passed | `admit(reply, ceiling)` takes the lock and reserves the call's ceiling; `spend` frees it. Proved: a new reservation admitted ⇒ charges + reservations ≤ limit; both steps preserve charges + reservations ≤ limit + `over` | `budget-boundary`, `budget-own-ceiling`, `budget-open-reservations`, `budget-no-hold`, `budget-held-twice`, `budget-recorded-admit`, `budget-release`, `budget-over`, plus the retargeted `budget-repeat`, `budget-total` |
| 4. Usage charged as zero (product bug) | `inputTokens ?? 0` made absent usage valid and free; an invalid report charged only the earlier valid calls | A usable provider total takes precedence; otherwise both component counts are required. Missing or malformed usage latches `usageValid = false`; provider failures observed by the reply and unusable reports charge the ceiling. Drafts and reviewers settle conservatively when the SDK reports no accounted calls or its meter fails | `reply-progress-domain-present`, `budget-unreported-free` |
| 5. Runs and walkthroughs | `apply`/`receive` never mentioned `runs` or `walkthrough`; `stepRun` and `decide`'s action arms proved nothing | `apply` frames `runs` and `walkthrough` on every other event, appends an exact `ActionRequested` run, and maps exactly `stepRun`/`settleRun` over the matching run; `receive` carries the run clauses; `stepRun` appends or updates exactly one step and keeps the run running; `decide` copies every action field, requires a fresh id, and numbers steps and settlements exactly for an open run | `steprun-drop-step`, `steprun-passed`, `apply-action-actor`, `apply-tour-end-runs`, `apply-walkthrough-guard`, `decide-request-copies`, `decide-trace-open`, `decide-settle-open` |
| 6. Sandbox metering | The proved accrual clause was vacuous at the host (`now` = `lastMeteredAt`); `meter`'s loop was unproved | Each interval's accrual and month rollover is the proved `meterStep`; `meter` supplies UTC boundaries and buckets. `decideSandbox`'s elapsed clause stays, labelled for what it is: admission, not billing | `meter-rollover-early`, `meter-rollover-carry`, `meter-step-count` |
| 7. Inventory | `decide.vibe` rows read "Not yet proved"; so did 60 `//@ verify` functions in `issueDecision`, `paneDecision`, `src/web/tourDecision` and `updateDecision` | Each of the five modules has a note; a regression fails if any function marked `//@ verify` in any production source is labelled unproved | inventory test |
| 8. Harness | Any callee's precondition counted as a rejection; imports were trusted unchecked | No callee-precondition rejection qualifies. Capacity cases have direct checked safety assertions. Every value dependency is freshly proved; unmarked contracts, external values and circular value-import assumptions are rejected | harness tests |
| 9. Restated contracts | Labelled "Proved" like real properties | Labelled "Specification restated" in the inventory (below) | none |

### What is still a boundary

- The budget's semaphore and the Durable Object's storage serialize a day's admissions; the proof is over the integer
  transitions, and the workerd suite exercises twenty concurrent admissions through the real object. A call that
  spends beyond its own ceiling (a provider overrunning its context window or answer limit) adds to `over`, logged
  and counted; the bound is charges ≤ limit + `over`, not charges ≤ limit.
- Every physical provider invocation reserves separately through the ordinary SDK Budget service. Its durable receipt charges usable final usage, or its ceiling for absent, invalid or incomplete usage. The answer is sealed before accounting; a ledger retry replays receipts without another provider call. A hard process kill before settlement conservatively retains that physical hold. An unconfigured reply holds nothing. The initial run reservation remains the fallback when tests replace the entire agent service.
- `meter`'s UTC month boundaries come from `Date.UTC`, and its loop's termination and bucket storage are host code.

The continuation adds missing-call tracking even after earlier known usage and marks reissued aggregate records incomplete. Physical billing uses separate receipts, so a later unknown call charges its own ceiling in addition to prior actual usage. Walkthrough controls have complete apply/receive frames; no callee-precondition exception remains.

### Specifications restated

These contracts are the policy table their body computes. They fix the meaning other proofs rely on and reject an
edit to the table, but prove no further property, nor that callers pass the right argument: `mayRun`, `runsOf`,
`wikiSubmissionAllowed`, `accountRoute`, `canCharge`, `chargeKeyOf`, `cookieName`, `localOrigin`, `cookieAccepted`,
`leastRoleOf`, `inputOf` and `postLabel`. The inventory labels each one so.

### Tool gaps fixed

- LemmaScript's contract parser rejected `??` (`Unexpected: {"type":"op","value":"?"}`), so no contract could read the
  optional `runs`. Fixed in `packages/lemmascript` (`specparser.ts`), with parser tests and the
  `spec-nullish.ts`/`spec-nullish-wrong.ts` fixture pair.
- `@smthrs/agent`'s `Budget.Usage` could not tell an unreported call from a free one (`tokensOf` reads a missing
  counter as zero). It now exports `reportsTokens` (safe nonnegative counters) and counts `Usage.unreported`, live and after recovery. App writers also charge their ceiling when no calls were accounted or the SDK meter is unavailable.
- `roleOf` and `apply` loop, so they cannot appear in a contract: `canGrant`'s self-grant clause uses the first-grant
  quantifier and `roleOf`'s witness clause, and `receive` restates `apply`'s run clauses.
- `receive`'s run clauses verify, but Dafny cannot refute a mutant of them inside the mutation gate's 30-second limit
  (a mutant that drops runs on `ActionRequested`, or on `Posted`, timed out on both the appended-run clause and the
  plain runs frame). They have no executable mutant; `apply`'s run mutants stand for the same relation, since
  `receive` applies `apply`. `apply-action-actor` names a short actor clause for the same reason.
- Dafny cannot relate the `.some(...)` LemmaScript emits (`exists run :: run in s`) to the index quantifiers the
  contracts use, so `decide` and `apply` look runs up through the proved loops `hasRun` and `hasOpenRun`.

## Fifth proofs lane (vl-proveall5): issue-graph acyclicity and replay equivalence

This lane proves the two obligations no other lane owned: no sequence of issue writes creates a cycle, and replaying a
journal reproduces exactly the state the live run reached. Its batches are numbered on their own.

### Fifth-lane batch 1: the issue graph stays a forest

An issue's one edge is its parent (GitHub sub-issues); the product has no other issue edge. `issueAncestorAt` and
`canLinkIssues` moved, contracts and bodies unchanged, from `conversation.vibe` to the new
`src/core/issueGraphDecision.vibe`, so the graph proofs see the measure's definition instead of an imported contract.

| Function | What its contract states | Called from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issuesAfter` | The issues after one accepted write: a created issue goes first, under the split issue or else at the root; any other write edits each issue with its number, and only a link changes a parent. From a forest, every write the host accepts leads to a forest: numbers stay positive, every parent is the root or an issue, and no issue is its own ancestor at any number of links. The premises are the host's checks: a created issue takes `nextIssueNumber`, a split's issue exists, and a link passed `canLinkIssues`, whose guarantee is the link premise word for word. | `src/core/IssuesFactory.vibe` (the mock's write) |
| `editedIssue` | Comment, commit, uncommit, link, accept and decline keep the issue's number; only a link changes its parent. | `issuesAfter` |
| `nextIssueNumber` | A created issue's number is positive and above every issue's number. | `src/core/IssuesFactory.vibe` |
| `issueCreates` | New, propose and split create an issue. | `src/core/IssuesFactory.vibe` |

How the proof goes: a link's new cycle would pass through the linked child, and the child's walk after the link is the
parent's old walk, which `canLinkIssues` proved reaches the root without passing the child (`issueLinkChildFree`,
`issueLinkAcyclic`). A walk that never stands on the child is unchanged (`issueLinkFrame`). A created issue's number
is fresh: no issue has it or names it as parent, so no old walk reaches it (`issueAvoids`, `issueAddFrame`). Every
other write keeps every edge (`issueSameEdges`). By induction over writes, no sequence of writes creates a cycle. The
specification-only lemmas never run; `verify/proof_additions.py` supplies their checked induction steps.

`test/issues.property.test.vibe` drives 60 random sequences of up to ten new, split, link, commit, uncommit and comment
writes through the real mock factory and checks the forest after each write. With the shell's `canLinkIssues`
check removed, it fails.

Boundary: the live Worker (`worker/Issues.vibe`) makes the same `canLinkIssues` check before it writes a link, and a
split there links a new GitHub issue under an existing one; GitHub then owns the edges. The proof covers the writes the
app decides, not GitHub's own state. An empty mock store would number its first issue 1, where `Math.max` gave
`-Infinity`; the shipped fixture store starts nonempty.

### Fifth-lane batch 2: replay reproduces the live run

| Module | What its contracts state | Called from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/core/replayDecision.vibe` | `replayLog` (moved from `conversation.vibe`, contract unchanged) is exactly the left fold `replayedLog` of `apply` over the log. `recordedConversation` is the sequencer's live step: an accepted event is applied and appended to the log, a refused intent changes neither, and while the conversation is the replay of its log it stays so. | `worker/Sequencer.vibe` (load and record), `src/core/MockFactory.vibe` (room load and record) |
| `src/history/replayDecision.vibe` | `replayHistory` (moved from `mythical.vibe`, contract unchanged) is exactly the left fold `replayedHistory` of `replayEvent`. `recordedHistory` is the history sequencer's live step: an accepted event moves the history exactly as replaying it does. `liveHistoryReplays`: while the live history is the replay of the journal, recording keeps it so, with the accepted event appended to the journal. | `src/history/Sequencer.vibe` (load and record) |

Composition at completed successful records: the Worker and history sequencers load by replaying the journal and
write an accepted event before setting the cached state. The mock updates its paired state/log in Ref.modify, writes
that log under its uninterruptible recorder gate, then publishes. Given serialized records and successful ordered
store writes, induction over the proved record cores makes the completed live state exactly the replay of its
retained journal. Cache/store atomicity during failures, interruption and crashes remains an Effect-shell boundary.
The mock's room load used
`retained.reduce(apply, empty)`; it now calls the proved `replayLog`, the same fold.

Inside these modules `apply`, `decide`, `decideWithinCapacity` and `replayEvent` are their proved contracts: LemmaScript
declares an imported function as a function with its contract, which is sound because each is deterministic code proved
in its own module. The folds use opaque total steps (`conversationStep`, `replayStep`) whose contracts say they equal
`apply` and `replayEvent` inside their domains, so the fold lemmas reason from shape alone. The conversation replay runs
with per-assertion isolation, as `conversation.vibe` and `decide.vibe` do: re-checking the well-formedness of `apply`'s
imported contract takes over 60 seconds as one batch.

Boundary: the store's durability and order, the lock and PubSub delivery are Effect runtime behavior, not proved.
