## Strengthening lane follow-up (vl-proof-strengthen, 2026-11-10)

### Strengthening follow-up: a transient ledger fault at a physical call

Per-call receipts moved the release of the run's hold into the provider boundary (`worker/CallBudget.vibe`). One
refused ledger request there failed the model call, so a reviewer answered `review` and a draft answered `draft`
although the ledger recovered at once. `test/specificationReviewers.coverage.test.vibe` and
`test/draftWriters.coverage.test.vibe` ("retries a charge the ledger refuses once") failed first. Each ledger request at
the boundary now retries three times (50 ms exponential) before it is reported unavailable. Admission holds a key once
and settlement charges a key once (`worker/budgetDecision.vibe`), so a retry never holds or charges twice. The test
ledger settles each key once, as production does, and the writers' tests count physical calls: every request that
reached the model is reserved and charged, including the agent's reissues.

The isolated positive proofs of `conversation.vibe` and `decide.vibe` took 2,274 s for `conversation.vibe` on a box,
and a fresh dependency proof inside the `decide` mutation group passed the 3,600 s wall. The wall only stops a hung
solver; it is now 7,200 s. Each obligation keeps its solver limit (60 s; 120 s for `conversation.vibe` and `decide.vibe`; 180 s for the history
replay module), and mutants keep 30 s (120 s
for four quantified walkthrough and pending clauses and the two replay loops, listed in `verify/mutation_targets.py`). A timeout still never counts as a
rejection.

### Strengthening follow-up: own failures and closed proof dependencies

`verify/check.py` includes every value dependency in its fresh strict typecheck and proof receipt. Negative runs first
prove the original dependencies, sequentially, then check the mutants; no imported body is accepted because its file is
merely marked. Cyclic value-import assumptions require a joint proof and are rejected. Copied value inputs are bound to the discovered source hashes. Dependency failures, timeouts and tool
errors stop the gate. `mutation_results.py` accepts only a direct own-contract diagnostic in the intended file and
function. The three history capacity cases use explicit checked safety assertions. No compiled application behavior
changes.

The inventory distinguishes a verify marker with no postcondition from a behavioral proof. Such a row says
“Checked without a behavioral postcondition”; currently the marked `tourWalkthrough` query and its callback have
that limited claim. The new apply/receive contracts specify walkthrough drive, pause, resume and seek projection,
invalid-step frames, and remaining-duration clamping. Fourteen executable mutants cover those relations.

The `canLinkIssues` relation (now in `src/core/issueGraphDecision.vibe`) states both directions: a positive child and parent with a present child are
accepted exactly when the first-match parent path reaches root within `items.length + 1` steps, every traversed node
exists, and none is the child. The extra loop prefix invariants distinguish an unknown node from a root and rule out
an earlier root on a still-running traversal. `issues-link-complete` replaces the final result with false. This is
acceptance completeness for that bounded path policy; preservation of an entire issue graph is a separate claim.

### Physical billing and adapter mutations

The SDK's optional `reserveCall`/`recordCall` pair guards each actual provider stream, including an in-step reissue.
The credential-free receipt and per-call usage are cached with the sealed answer; settlement then runs idempotently,
on replay too. An accounting failure after sealing cannot dispatch another provider call. A failed unsealed call
also reconciles its receipt, and a process killed before that write leaves the ceiling held. The app uses this guard
for replies, VIP drafts, wiki drafts and each specification reviewer. The run's initial one-call hold is handed off
to physical receipts; an unavailable or wholly replaced agent still has that initial conservative fallback.

`runtime_mutations.py`, imported by the registry in `mutations.py`, names lock removal, missing usage accepted as
zero, and a sandbox host passing its old clock. `runtime_broken.py` runs a passing production baseline and then
requires an assertion failure in the intended behavioral regression. Compiler errors, startup failures and timeouts
do not qualify. The default `verify:broken` gate runs this registry after Dafny; runtime counts stay separate.

### Strengthening follow-up: rebased onto the fifth and third lanes

The fifth and third lanes' modules met this lane's stricter rejection rule on rebase. These harness changes
followed:

- `proof_diagnostics.py` found a failure's enclosing declaration with a pattern that skipped `opaque function`, so
  `conversation-step-applies` failed the opaque `conversationStep`'s own postcondition and was refused as "no direct
  own-contract failure". It now uses `sources.enclosing_symbol`
  (`test_a_postcondition_of_an_opaque_function_is_its_own_failure`, which failed first).
- One isolated `receive` obligation of `conversation.vibe`'s 14,905 timed out at 60 s in three of six box runs and
  proved in the other three, stopping the positive gate and two mutation groups' dependency proofs.
  `PROOF_TIME_LIMITS` gives `conversation.vibe` 120 s per positive obligation, as the third lane also found; mutants
  keep their budgets (`test_conversation_headroom_is_positive_only`). A timeout still never counts as proved.
- `history-fold-prefix` and `myth-fold-prefix` fail `apply`'s own checked fold assertion, but the whole unisolated
  `apply` also timed out at 30 s, so the run did not qualify. `ASSERTIONS` now checks that one assertion alone.

- Dafny reports a failed quantified postcondition in a function's contract lemma as "possible violation of
  postcondition of forall statement". `mock-actor-key-sep` failed `actorKey`'s own contract that way and was refused;
  that wording now counts as a postcondition (`test_a_quantified_contract_lemma_failure_is_a_postcondition`, which
  failed first).
- A mutant's Dafny process may run 1,800 s before it is stopped as hung (`wall_limit`). `apply`'s targeted
  walkthrough clauses are checked on every return path, each within its solver limit, and eight passed 600 s in total.
  `apply-drive-range` and `apply-tour-end-runs` get the 120 s clause budget of their sibling frame clauses. A stopped
  process or a timeout still never counts.
- `sandbox-replace-append` replaced the appended entry with `entries[0]`, which Dafny refused only as an out-of-range
  index on an empty ledger. It now appends a copy of the first entry when there is one, so `replaceSandbox`'s own
  append assertion must refute it.
- `test/writerAccounting.coverage.test.vibe` (main) counted one `reply/` charge per answered writer. Each physical
  provider call now has its own `reply/model/` receipt, so it checks one run charge plus one receipt per scripted call;
  `spent` and `reserved` assertions are unchanged.

The walkthrough and `issues-link-complete` cases moved from `mutations.py` to `extended_mutations.py`, so the fifth
lane's `test_every_time_limit_names_a_mutation` covers their time limits. `issues-link-complete` now targets
`src/core/issueGraphDecision.vibe`, where `canLinkIssues` moved.

## Schema Model translation (lane vl-lemmascript-model)

The page's `Model` is an Effect Schema value type (`type Model = typeof Model.Type`), and LemmaScript could not read
it: the six-line probe in `~/vl/vibelang-bugs/lemmascript-schema-model-translation/` emitted
`type Schema.optionalKey(==)`, a Dafny parse error, and `seq<i__type>` array elements. The fix is in the tool
(`packages/lemmascript`, README patch table): field types come from the value type the TypeScript checker resolves,
never the schema's declaration text. Anonymous objects, array elements, record values and tagged unions become named
datatypes; structurally equal types share one, so `Model.account` and `AccountState` are one datatype; an
`optionalKey` is `Option` under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`; a brand is its primitive.

The probe now verifies with no cast or opaque declaration (1/1, exit 0). `src/web/modelWrite.vibe` moves the Model
half of two translation helpers into proofs over the real `Model`:

| Function | Contract | Called from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `writeAccount` | The next Model is the old one with `surface`, `docs` and the account's nine screen fields from the step, over the current account (or `signedOut`); every other Model and account field is unchanged. | `runAccount` (14 account arms) |
| `writeActions` | The next Model is the old one with the panel's nine screen fields from the step, over the current panel (or `initial`); every other Model and panel field is unchanged. | `runActions` (6 actions arms) |

13 mutations in `verify/arm_mutations.py` (`write-account-*`, `write-actions-*`). Still boundaries:
Foldkit command construction (`accountCommand`, `actionCommand`: a Foldkit `Command` is not plain data), `runEscape`
and `runTourControl`, which `test/translation.property.test.vibe` still checks. The `update` arms themselves belong to
`vl-proveall`, whose unlanded LemmaScript chain changes the same `extract.ts` and must keep one structural-type
mechanism when it rebases.

## Per-mutant wall budget (lead decision, 2026-11-10)

The lead, as the gate's owner, ruled that a mutant's wall budget is a resource limit, not a correctness threshold, and
raised it to at least 300 s. `verify/mutation_targets.py` `wall_limit` (vl-proof-strengthen, "Strengthening lane
follow-up") already gives a mutant 1,800 s and an isolated proof 7,200 s, so the ruling holds with no further change.
Measurements behind it: `apply-action-actor` (`src/core/conversation.vibe` `apply`) is rejected by its contract in 117 s
alone on a 2-core box, hit 180 s beside another mutant in two full `verify:broken` runs (the only one of 1,660 and 1,903
that did not finish; none survived), and hit 300 s (311 s) beside 58 other mutants and a full proof run on nyc-01 at load
~160 (2026-11-11). 300 s does not hold under that load; 1,800 s does. No contract or mutant changed.

## Third-lane batch 21: the API Worker's object bodies

`worker/apiObjects.vibe`, the bodies of the API Worker's Durable Objects and its fetch handler, made its choices
inline. They now live in `worker/apiObjectDecision.vibe`; every `apiObjects.vibe` inventory row is proved or forwards.

| Function | What its contract states |
| --- | --- |
| `actionRoot` | A reply run `<id>-reply` lives in `<id>`'s conversation (`\result + "-reply" == id`); any other id is its own |
| `answered`, `pendingPost` | The alarm answers the first person's post with no finished reply: every earlier entry is an agent's or answered; -1 when none is pending |
| `readsPostOwner`, `alarmOwner`, `alarmName`, `alarmAgent` | The stored post owner is read only when no request names an owner and a post is pending. The alarm acts for the request's owner, else the post's, else nobody (`""`); under the request's name, else the post's, else `Guest`; as an agent unless a person's request started it |
| `crossOriginRefused`, `recordsParticipation` | A signed-in post or history write from another origin is refused; a visitor's never is. Only an accepted post by a signed-in person records participation |
| `writeActor` | A visitor writes as a viewer named Guest, never an agent; a person keeps their role, login and agent flag (unset is a person) |
| `sandboxRole` | The account role only when the sandbox permission admits the caller, else viewer; the shell reads the role only once admitted |
| `draftForbidden`, `signedOutRoute`, `bootstrapsHistory` | An owner-less agent draft is refused before any RPC. With sign-in unconfigured only `/api/issues` and `/api/wiki` are served. The History object seeds from main only at seq 0 |

`test/apiObjectDecision.test.vibe` failed first against stub bodies (7 of 7). 18 Dafny obligations; 29 mutations.
Behavior is unchanged: the alarm still reads the stored owner only when the request has none and a post is pending,
and the sandbox role is still read only for an admitted caller. Stub lookup, RPC transport, storage, layers, the
action host and SSE remain host boundaries.

## Third-lane batch 22: main's commit order, over Map and Set

`worker/MainLog.vibe` `newCommits`, the commits a live fold takes from GitHub's listing of main, walked a commit graph
with a `Map` and two `Set`s, a tool boundary until LemmaScript could state one. It now calls
`worker/mainLogDecision.vibe` `newCommitOrder`, which returns indices into the listing; the shell formats them.

| Function | What its contract states |
| --- | --- |
| `lastIndexBySha` | Each listed id maps to an index holding it, and every listed id is a key (the last index, as `new Map(entries)` keeps) |
| `isCursor`, `firstParent` | The cursor is a nonempty prefix of an id. A commit's first parent is the listed commit with that id, else -1 when unlisted (no parent looks up `""`) |
| `sideShas` | A merge brings in only listed ids, none taken before, on the first-parent line or the cursor. It terminates: each step adds a new key to the group, so `bySha.keys() - group` shrinks |
| `groupOrder` | A group's commits, each once at its own index, strictly newest listed first, and every member present |
| `newCommitOrder` | No listing: `[]` for an empty cursor, else `undefined`; the head at the cursor: `[]`. A defined answer holds listed indices, no id twice, none at the cursor, the head last; with a cursor, some listed commit is it; without one, it includes the commit whose first parent is unlisted |
| `pageAccepted`, `readsAnotherPage` | Only status 200 is a page. Another page is read only after a full one and below `MAX_PAGES` |

Behavior: on every real listing the order is the replaced one. `test/mainLogOrder.test.vibe` keeps the replaced code
verbatim as the reference and compares 3,000 generated cases (DAGs up to 18 commits, cut to a page, overlapping pages,
five kinds of cursor). One deliberate change: a listing whose first parents meet a commit twice, which no git history
has, now answers `undefined` (the fold reads on, then reports main out of reach); the replaced walk never ended. The
test generator first padded ids so that `c1` and `c10` collided, and the replaced walk ran until its array overflowed;
the generator now writes fixed-width ids.

18 Dafny obligations across the module; 18 mutations, two of them (`main-order-cycle`, `main-order-unreached`) added
after the first contract let them through, and the contract strengthened until both were rejected.

LemmaScript gaps fixed in `packages/lemmascript`, each with tests (`tools/tests/map-set.test.ts`, fixture
`tools/fixtures/map-set.ts` checked by Dafny in `test-fixtures.sh`) and a README row:

| Gap | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `k in m ==> items[m[k]] == k` typed `m[k]` as an Option in an index position | A `k in m` on the left of `&&`/`==>` narrows the right, as an `if` does |
| A contract could not name a map's keys, so a graph walk had no termination measure | A contract's `m.keys()` is Dafny `m.Keys`; `decreases m.keys() - seen` proves the walk ends. Code keeps it unmodeled (an ordered iterator) |
| `\result != undefined && \result.length == 0` emitted `|f(b)|` over an Option, ill-typed | A boolean `&&` binds a present value on its right; a top-level contract conjunction is split only before its first guard. Premises, conditions, longer chains and a right side that already matches on the value keep their rules. The first version broke `conversation.vibe`'s `WalkthroughDriven` contract (`x != undefined && (x ?? d) == d`), caught by the full gate; the regression test is that shape |
| `(r.w ?? { step: 1 })` in a contract typed the literal default as the function's return type, not the field's | A record or array literal default of `??` builds the left operand's type |

## Third-lane batch 24: RegExp tests, and the history's first proved patterns

LemmaScript now proves `pattern.test(s)` for a literal pattern, or a module `const` holding one
(`packages/lemmascript/tools/src/regex.ts`). The pattern becomes a Dafny regular-expression term. A derivative matcher
decides it, and two lemmas, re-proved in every file that tests a pattern, tie the matcher to the pattern's language:
`JsMatchCorrect` (matcher equals language membership) and `JsTestCorrect` (`test` equals "some substring with the
anchored ends is in the language"). A contract names a test with `\matches("pattern", s)`.

The subset: UTF-16 code units, `.`, classes with ranges and `\d \w \s` and their negations, groups, alternation,
`* + ? {m} {m,} {m,n}` (greedy or lazy: `test` answers the same), `^` first and `$` last, no flags. A flag, `\b`, a
lookaround, a backreference, and `exec`, `match`, `replace` or `split` with a pattern are refused by name. The parser's
semantics equals the native `RegExp` on 19 patterns, every in-subset pattern of the history and wiki scripts among them,
times 412 strings each (`tools/tests/regex.test.ts`). The minimal reproduction `verify/bugs/regexp.ts` proves now and
was removed.

| Function | What its contract states |
| --- | --- |
| `sentenceEnded` (seedDecision, called by `seed.vibe` `endsSentence`) | Exactly `\matches("[.!?][\"'`)\\]]*$", text)`; the empty text ends nothing |
| `ownsLine` (seedDecision, called by `evidenceOf`) | Exactly the own-line pattern (a `Key:`, a bullet or a numbered item); the empty line owns nothing |
| `trailerLine`, `trailerParagraph` (`src/history/trailerDecision.vibe`, called by `Sequencer.vibe` `trailerOf`) | A `Key:` line, or after the first line one that starts with a space or tab; the empty line is neither. A paragraph is a trailer exactly when every line is a trailer line at its own position |

`test/regexDecisions.test.vibe` failed first against stubs (3 of 3) and compares each decision with the replaced literal
on 5,000 generated strings. 9 mutations, 4 of them edits to a pattern, are rejected by the contracts that pin each pattern.

Still outside the subset, each with its reason in the inventory: `REGENERATED` (`\b`), `sanitize` (`\b` and `replace`),
`titleOf` and `wholeSentences` (`replace`), `scopeOf` and `evidenceOf`'s capture (`exec`), `trailerOf`'s line splits and
its `Mythical:` capture (`split`, `replace`, `exec`), and the wiki script's `exec`, `match`, `replace` and two `i`-flag
tests. They need explicit string decisions, or an `exec` capture model in LemmaScript.

## Spec functions in the harness (vl-ghost-functions, 2026-11-10)

A function that only states a proof, such as `runningCountPrefix`, is compiled, exported and counted by coverage. VIP-43
gives it a form: a `spec function` erases from JavaScript and declarations, and EK4310 rejects any runtime reference.
The harness reads a `.vibe` module as TypeScript, so each staged copy writes `spec function` as `export function` on
the same line, as VibeLang's own lowering does (VIP-43 Appendix F, "The lowering file"). Lines keep their numbers.

| Piece | Where | Test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A staged source, staged import or mutant writes `spec function` as `export function` | `verify/spec_functions.py`, `check.py`, `mutations.py` | `harness_test.SpecFunctions` |
| A mutation finds a spec function's span | `verify/mutation_edit.py` | `test_a_spec_function_is_found_and_ends_at_the_next_function` |

The app declares no spec function yet: the compiler does not parse the form. When a VibeLang release does,
`runningCountPrefix`, `restartsBefore` and `issueKnownAction` become spec functions and
`test/decisionEdges.coverage.test.vibe` loses the tests that only covered them.

## Proof reuse (vl-proveall, 2026-11-11)

A value import makes the callee's contracts axioms of the caller, so since the strengthening lane a run proves the
callee fresh, and its whole value-import tree with it. That is sound, and slow: one module that imports
`conversation.vibe` costs its isolated proof every time (2,016 s for `modelWrite.vibe` with two value imports, against
33 s without).

`verify/proof_cache.py` now stores a module's passing result under a key over everything that decides it, and a run
reuses it while the key is unchanged:

| Key part | Why |
| --- | --- |
| The module's app path; whether the app's checked proof steps apply | `proof_additions.py` inserts steps by path |
| Every file TypeScript loads for the staged module, by path and content (`verify/proof_inputs.cjs`: one program per root, with the run's tsconfig, as `lsc gen` finds it) | its own copy, imported copies, emitted declarations, packages and libraries: a change to any re-proves it, and a callee's change re-proves each importer |
| TypeScript and ts-morph versions | LemmaScript parses with them |
| LemmaScript's build (`tools/dist`), Dafny's version string (which pins its Z3) | the tools |
| The run's LemmaScript settings, without the run folder | string semantics, library |
| Every Python module the run loaded from `verify/`, the Node scripts and the install scripts | the harness decides flags, limits and proof steps |

The run folder and checkout path are replaced by placeholders before hashing. A mutant is always proved, a failed
proof is never stored, and a pass is stored only when every non-mutant module of the run passed, so no stored pass
leans on a callee that failed. `VERIFY_FRESH=1` ignores the store. `harness_test.py`'s `ProofReuse` cases failed
first: an unchanged rerun re-proved both modules; now it proves none, a changed callee re-proves it and its importer,
a changed importer re-proves only itself, `VERIFY_FRESH=1` proves both, a failed proof is proved again on every run,
and a changed LemmaScript build changes the key.

Measured on a box (`g1`, batch 48): `pnpm verify:broken` over the 11 `write-scope-*` mutants reused both dependency
modules (`screenRead.vibe`, `updateDecision.vibe`) that the preceding `pnpm verify src/web/modelWrite.vibe` stored, and
proved only the mutants (59.5 s).

Measured on a box (`c1`, the cache commit's tree): `python3 verify/check.py src/core/tourDecision.vibe`, which
imports `conversation.vibe`, took 1,846.2 s cold (2/2 proved) and 2.98 s on the unchanged rerun (2/2 reused).

## Third-lane batch 36: main's buckets for the mythical bootstrap

`bucketsOf` groups every commit main's tip reaches under the first-parent step that brought it in. It walked each
step's side ancestry depth-first with a `Set` of seen commits and `spine.includes`, then sorted each side by index.
`src/history/bucketDecision.vibe` (new) replaces the walk with index arithmetic over parent indexes, which the
generator's `jj log --reversed` order makes parents-first:

| Function | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `topological` | Exactly: every parent index is -1 or below its child |
| `mainLine` | The tip is on main; a main commit's first parent is on main; every other main commit has a main child whose first parent it is |
| `takesOwner` | Exactly: a parent takes an owner when it is off main and has no owner or a larger one |
| `owners` | A main commit owns itself; an owned commit's owner is a main commit at or above it; no parent link off main reaches a commit from a smaller owner (closure); every owned commit off main has a parent link from a commit with the same owner (witness). Closure and witness make the owner exactly the oldest main commit that reaches the commit without passing through main |
| `chains` | Each owner's commits linked oldest first; a link skips no commit of the same owner, and an owner's head is its oldest |
| `bucketed` | Every bucket names an owned commit and its owner; buckets strictly ascend by owner, then commit; every owned commit stands at a recorded position |
| `bucketOrder` | Composes the three; buckets ascend by step, then commit, and no commit is above its step |

The old walk took a side commit for the oldest step that reached it, stopping at main and at commits already taken;
a commit taken earlier is reached by that earlier step too, so stopping there never changes the oldest reacher. The
proved owner is that oldest reacher. `test/bucketDecision.test.vibe` keeps the old walk as an oracle and checks
equal output on 300 generated histories with merges and outside parents.

One behavior changed, on purpose: a list whose parents do not come first now has no buckets (the old walk followed
shas in any order). The generator always lists parents first. The sweep is linear in commits and parent links; the
old walk's `spine.includes` was linear per side commit, and the first proved draft (per-step sweeps with `.with`
copies) was quadratic, about 50 million steps on VibeLang's 7,075 commits.

The wiki link fold had only invariants (no empty or `.` segment, `..` only after `..`), so two of batch 34's
mutants survived it (`wiki-link-parent-climb`: `..` removed a `..`; `wiki-link-parent-kept`: a leading `..` dropped).
Its contract is now exact: `foldSegment` states each segment's result, the recursive `foldedPrefix` folds the first
`count` segments and carries the invariants, and `resolvedSegments` equals `foldedPrefix` over every segment.

Mutation: 18 new mutants (`bucket-*`; owners passing `false` for a parent on main is equivalent and not listed). The one-parent step is its own function, `takesOwner`, with an exact contract,
and `bucketed`'s list building is `chains`: inside the larger loops their mutants timed out at the 30-second budget
under host load instead of failing a contract; the fold's mutants (`wiki-link-dot`, `wiki-link-parent-climb`,
`wiki-link-parent-kept`) now aim at `foldSegment`, and `wiki-link-fold-skip` (the first segment skipped) is new.

Main's `splitCommand` (`Actions.vibe`, #5341: a slash command keeps its text as typed) arrived during the rebase. Its
cut is the proved `commandCut` (`actionHostDecision.vibe`; mutants `action-cut-*`); the live and mock hosts call it,
then the proved `firstCommand` and `commandInput`.

LemmaScript gap fixed on the way: `return bucketed(owner).order` emitted a method call inside an expression, which
Dafny rejects. A field read's object now lifts to a bind like a call argument (`tools/tests/field-lift.test.ts`).

No row of `src/core`, `src/actions`, `src/history`, `src/surfaces` or `scripts/` reads "Not yet proved".

## Batch 52 (vl-proveall, 2026-11-12): the Model write of an applied event

`ReceivedEvent` decided through the proved `eventReceived` already; the Model it wrote was inline. `eventWrite` now
states it: the screen step (`completeScreenTour`) over the Model, the client, the connection and announced count the
plan names, the answer `answerAnnouncement` chose, and exactly the five planned parts: the sandbox pane minimized
(`minimizedSandbox`), a plain page ready with no follow-up, a wiki page ready and no longer followed with the follow-up
`wikiAfterEvent` chose, the editor closed, the People pane docked; every other field unchanged. A replay plan keeps its
own write (client resumed, epoch, from). 9 mutations (`write-event-*`).

Tool gap found and fixed: two conditional spreads that write the same field (`wikiStatus` and `wikiAfter`, for a
plain page and a wiki page) left two updates of it, which Dafny refuses (`duplicate update member`). A field written
again now replaces the earlier entry, whose value the new one holds as its fallback (`spread-same-field.ts`, red
before, its wrong twin fails a postcondition).

Tool gap recorded: `NonNullable<Model["sandboxPane"]>` over an optional string-literal union emits an abstract
`NonNullable<Option<string>>` (`~/vl/vibelang-bugs/lemmascript-nonnullable-string-union/`); the write names the
declared `SandboxPane` instead, the same type.

Not proved yet: fourteen arms still write the Model inline, most one field from a proved decision. They are

`UpdatedTerminal`, `FilteredWiki`, the replay plan in `ReceivedEvent`, `FailedEvents` and `ClickedReconnect`.

## Third-lane batch 37: three new worker shells and the whole gate on boxes

**Scope.** Main added three shells after the last full inventory: `worker/sandboxBenchmark.vibe` (the test-stage
counter export), `worker/SubmissionBase.vibe` (a submission's persisted source) and `worker/ReplyAccounting.vibe`
(a reply's token receipts and their settlement), 12 rows "Not yet proved". Each now calls a proved decision:

| Decision | Module | What the proof states |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `benchmarkPath`, `benchmarkAnswer` | `sandboxWorkerDecision` | Only `/api/probe/coverage` reaches the export; no owner is forbidden before the method is read; only an owner's POST reads the counters. |
| `submissionStep` | `workerDecision` | With no storage the source is observed each time; a stored base is decoded and never observed again; otherwise it is observed, then recorded. |
| `receiptReported`, `settledReported` | `workerDecision` | Only a model reply's receipt waits for its usage; settlement closes a receipt as reported when its usage was reported or its admission never answered. |
| `cleanupStep`, `driveRewakes` | `workerDecision` | A live settlement flow's outcome is returned as is; a settled or forgotten one re-arms the main alarm, and only a forgotten one goes on to the main drive; a settled main drive re-arms the alarm. |

14 new mutants, all rejected (`verify:broken --module` both modules). The shells keep URL parsing, storage, Schema
decoding, alarms and the ExecutionObject calls. The inventory has 0 rows "Not yet proved".

**Box gate.** `pnpm verify` and `verify:broken` ran sharded by file on `cfbox --image node26` boxes (4 vCPU, 12 GB,
Dafny 4.11.0, at most 4 at once). Two findings, neither a proof that no longer holds:

- `record-journal-order` was refuted in 26.5 s at main `f7acadfa` and timed out at the 30 s mutant limit at
  `1b8ba47b` (37.5 s), after `conversation.vibe` grew. It gets the same 120 s headroom as the other record-equality
  counterexamples in `mutation_targets.py`. A timeout is still a tool failure, never a rejection.
- A box host restart (Cloudflare's SIGTERM, `cf-compute/OPERATIONS.md`) stopped one shard per run. The gate driver
  reruns an interrupted shard, at most twice, and never counts it as a verdict.

## Third-lane batch 38: an action follow's contracts that a body returning nothing met

`src/web/actionFollowDecision.vibe` (main `f7771264`) was proved but had no mutants. Its first 17 mutants left 4
survivors: `settled` and `watching` returning `[]`, or dropping `running` from their live test, met every
postcondition. Two clauses close the gap:

| Function | Added postcondition |
| --- | --- |
| `settled` | Every uncertain run without a terminal receipt stays uncertain. |
| `watching` | Every queued or running run that is not stopped is watched. |

`watching`'s clause needs a filter-then-map step (`proof_additions.py`). The step is guarded by the body's own
shape rather than asserted, so a mutated body skips it and fails the lemma's own postcondition, the only failure
`verify:broken` counts. 17/17 mutants rejected; 15 obligations verified.

## The box-only `harness_test.py` red (vl-proveall, 2026-11-13)

`python3 verify/harness_test.py` failed 10 tests and 2 errors in a `node26` box and passed 61 on the host. Two
preconditions that `pnpm verify` sets up were missing, because the gate ran the file alone:

- `run-heavy --add` delivers `verify/.tools/bin/lsc` as a copied file, which can't resolve `ts-morph`
  (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`); `check.sh` runs `lsc_fresh.py` to restore the link before the harness, a bare run did not.
  9 failures and 1 error.
- A fresh tree has no `src/assets/wiki.generated.vibe` or `wikiIndex.generated.vibe` (`pnpm wiki:build` writes them);
  the host kept them from an earlier build. Emitting `main.vibe`'s declarations failed on that import. 1 failure, 1 error.

The image is not at fault. `harness_test.py`'s `setUpModule` now runs `lsc_fresh.main()` and stops with one message
naming the missing generated modules; `test_a_tree_without_the_generated_wiki_modules_is_named` checks the names.
Checked in a `node26` box: a bare run before `wiki:build` stops on that message, and after it all tests pass.

## Third-lane batch 39: a mutant name used twice ran once

`mutations.py` keys the manifest and the mutant files by name. `route-wiki` named a `protocolDecision` case and a
`apiObjectDecision` case, so an unsharded `verify:broken` wrote 2,879 mutants for 2,880 cases and never ran the first.
A run by module ran both. `mutations.py` now stops on a duplicate name, so `MutationRegistry` (the `--check` run) fails
first; the worker case is `api-route-wiki`. Both mutants rejected.

## Landing check (vl-proveall3, 2026-11-13)

"0 rows not proved" held only for the revision a proof run saw. Before this change, `pnpm test` ran no inventory
check, and `land-main` runs no tests, so three things reached `main` unrefused: a row "Not yet proved" (ReplyAccounting
gained 10 between two full runs), a generated table that no longer matched its sources (main `a54642d6` held one:
`src/web/main.vibe` and `src/core/sandboxHost.vibe` had moved), and a new contract with no mutation case.

`verify/landing.cjs` refuses all of them, from the inventory, `mutations.py`'s case list and a typecheck of its
mutants, never Dafny (about 55 s):

| Refusal | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `not proved: <file>:<line> <name>` | Any inventory row whose reason starts "Not yet proved" |
| `stale inventory` | The 0018 table differs from `node verify/inventory.cjs`'s output |
| `no mutant: <file>:<line> <name>` | A top-level `//@ verify` function with a contract and no case in `mutations.py` (`--cases`) |
| `stale mutation: <case>` | A case whose text no longer matches its source exactly once (`mutations.py OUT --check`) |
| `unrecorded branch: <file>:<line> <function>` | A branch in a shell row that `verify/shell-branches.tsv` does not record ("Decisions in shell rows", below) |
| `invalid mutant: <case> (<file> <function>): <diagnostic>` | A case whose mutant no longer typechecks (`verify/mutant_types.py`) |

Exempt from `no mutant`: a lemma, whose executable body is `return true` or `return <base> ? true : <itself>(...)`, so
a mutant has nothing to change; and a contract whose reason is "Specification restated". A function marked `//@ verify`
with no contract is checked for its callees' preconditions and needs no case. The first run found 30 contracts with
none; each got one case (lane vl-proveall3 block in `mutations.py`).

It runs in two places:

- `pnpm test` runs `pnpm test:proofs` (`verify/inventory_test.cjs`, `verify/landing_test.cjs`). The regression adds an
  unproved decision to the real tree and sees it refused; fixtures cover each refusal and each exemption.
- `~/vl/bin/land-main` runs it on the final tip, after any rebase, under the lock, with `--check` too, for every range
  touching `apps/vibelang/`. It exits 7 on a refusal, and when the working copy is not on the tip (`jj new <tip>`).
  Scenarios 10 to 12 in `land-main.test.sh`.

To fix a refusal: prove the row (contract and mutation case), or give its inventory reason; run
`node verify/inventory.cjs --write`; rerun `node verify/landing.cjs`.

**Invalid mutants (2026-11-14).** `400d0ee8` narrowed `LoadActions.epoch` to `number`, so `actions-click-epoch`'s
mutant `epoch: null` stopped typechecking. The case's text still matched once, so the landing check passed, and
`verify:broken` stopped at the typecheck of the whole batch: 257 mutants voided, a full gate run on `cf4c78264e3e`
stopped and rerun. Now `check.py`, in a mutation run, charges each diagnostic to its file: a diagnostic in a mutant
marks that mutant invalid (exit 3, never proved) and the rest of the batch runs; a diagnostic anywhere else still stops
the run. `broken.py` judges every result and fails with one line per mutant not rejected (`INVALID`, `SURVIVED`,
`MISSING`) and the counts, instead of stopping at the first. The landing check typechecks every mutant in strict
programs of 500 (`verify/mutant_types.py`: 3,027 mutants in 7 programs, 40 s on nyc-02, two programs at a time; one
program over all of them peaked at 2.5 GB and ran out of heap on a box) and refuses each invalid one. The landing check
went from about 15 s to 55 s. Regression tests: `harness_test.py` `InvalidMutants` (an ill-typed mutant beside a valid one:
the valid one is proved and rejected, the ill-typed one is named invalid and never reaches Dafny; diagnostics are
charged to their own file; every unrejected mutant is named) and `landing_test.cjs` "a mutant that no longer
typechecks is refused by name". Putting `epoch: null` back makes `node verify/landing.cjs` refuse
`invalid mutant: actions-click-epoch (src/web/modelDecision.vibe clickedActions): ... TS2322`.

"Open" rows are decisions that hold no row of their own and are not "Not yet proved", so the row check cannot
see them; the branch record below can. They are the next proof batches, in the order above (authority first). The audit scripts and their full
output (file, line, row, condition) are in the lane report (`~/vl/vl-proveall3.REPORT.md`, nyc-01).

### The branch record and its refusal

`verify/branches.cjs` lists every `if` and conditional in a row that is not proved, outside the view markup in
`src/web/`, that has an operand (split at `&&`, `||` and `!`) no proof decides. An operand is decided when it calls a
proved function, reads a `const` that calls one (in its row or an enclosing one) as a flag or against a literal
(`replay === "replay-refused"`, `cut < 0`: the proved function's own answer), or is a presence or variant
test or a host type guard (`=== undefined`, `null`, `_tag`, `typeof`, `Option.isSome`, `Exit.isSuccess`,
`Number.isSafeInteger` and the like), which the audit found decide nothing of their own. So
`url.origin !== setup.origin || !writeOriginAdmitted(...)` is a shell branch (the origin comparison), and
`body === undefined || !runIdValid(body.id)` is not. The inventory's own parse records each row's branches, so the
landing check costs no second parse (about 13 s in all). `verify/shell-branches.tsv` records each one as file,
function (callback lines dropped, so moved code still matches), condition and reason; the landing check refuses a
branch it does not record, and a record with no reason. To land a new branch in a shell row: call a proved function
in its condition, or add the line the refusal prints with a reason. A reason starting `Open:` is a decision still to
prove: its count is the open-candidate count. `node verify/branches.cjs` prints the counts; `--prune` drops records
no branch matches (a proved condition leaves its record stale; stale records are not refused).

| Reason | Records after batch 47 (superseded below) |
| --- | ---: |
| `Open:` `signin.vibe`, `sandboxHost.vibe`, `commands.vibe`, `export.vibe`, `seed.vibe` (no worker site is open) | 119 |
| `Forwards`, `Metric only` or `Host boundary`, each with its reason | 7 |
| `Unreviewed`: recorded by the audit with no disposition yet | 498 |
| Total | 624 |

After batch 50 (417 branches; the literal-read rule took 157 of them):

| Reason | Records |
| --- | ---: |
| `Open:` | 0 |
| `Variant dispatch` or `Variant test`: a status, mode, kind or answer union picks its arm, each named | 24 |
| `Host boundary`: container state, Effect's Cause shape, Set and Map membership | 10 |
| `Formatting`: output text only | 10 |
| `Forwards`, `Metric only`, `Absence`: each with its reason | 13 |
| `Unreviewed`: recorded by the audit with no disposition yet | 360 |
| Total | 417 |

The 360 unreviewed records are branches the 2026-11-13 audit found outside the candidate groups (most in

## Batch 46 (vl-proveall3, 2026-11-13): request body limits

Five shells compared `Number(content-length)` with a literal: accounts 2,048 bytes (sign-in and roles), issues 32 KiB,
wiki 4 MiB, and a tour control's text 1,024 UTF-16 units; issues and wiki answered GET and POST only. In
workerDecision: `bodyLimit` (each route's limit, also the bounded read's `MaxBodySize`), `withinBodyLimit` (`!(length >
maximum)`: an absent or unparsable `content-length`, `NaN`, is read through the bounded read, as before) and
`objectMethod`. Six mutation cases (each limit, the boundary, POST). `test/workerDecision.test.vibe` pins the limits,
the boundary and `NaN`.

## Batch 54 (vl-proveall3, 2026-11-13): the meter's domain, a pending flow's expiry, the publisher's pacing

Of the 34 reviewed rules batch 53 left, eight are now proved. sandboxDecision proves `meterCount` (never negative),
`addsSafely` (an addition stays a safe integer) and `dateMilliseconds` (a JavaScript date), which the sandbox meter's
five guards call beside the host's `Number.isSafeInteger` and `isFinite`; signinDecision proves `pendingExpired`
(`session.vibe` drops a device flow at its expiry); the publisher's two pacing tests call the proved `pacedOut` and
`waitsForTrees`. Four mutation cases.

The wiki's body limit is now 8 MiB (`bodyLimit`, from 4 MiB): a save carries the page twice, as base and text, and
0018 reached 2,094,066 bytes, so `wikiEdit.http.test`'s "the largest actual wiki page fits the bounded edit request"
answered 413 (unit gate u54). The mutant for the limit is the old 4 MiB. Records: 363 branches, 0 open, 0 unreviewed, 26 reviewed rules not yet proved.

## Batch 55 (vl-proveall3, 2026-11-14): the last 26 reviewed rules

Each of the 26 reviewed rules batch 54 left is now proved or recorded as no decision. 20 branches call a proved
function and leave the record; 6 records now state why the branch decides nothing.

| Rule | Where | Proved function (module) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A write with no request key is sign-in | `Issues.vibe`, `Wiki.vibe` | `writeKeyMissing` (issueHostDecision) |
| The agent's login sorts first among assignee choices; localeCompare orders the rest | `Issues.vibe` read | `agentFirst` |
| A split links its new issue only when GitHub has not | `Issues.vibe` split | `splitLinkNeeded` |
| A link writes only a changed parent | `Issues.vibe` link | `parentChanges` |
| A wiki draft: a blank ask is empty, before a missing writer is unavailable | `Wiki.vibe` draft | `wikiDraftRefusal` |
| The pinned commit's page must equal the reviewed base | `Wiki.vibe` propose | `pinnedConflict` |
| The retained draft is deleted only when it holds the proposed text | `Wiki.vibe` propose | `draftProposed` |
| A conversation id is 1 to MAX_CONVERSATION units | `wire.vibe` `conversationPath` | the existing `validConversationLength` (protocolDecision) |
| A Fold's refusals before planning: empty, too-long, duplicate, in `decide`'s order | `Sequencer.vibe` fold | `foldRefusal` (mythical) |
| XDG_CONFIG_HOME wins, else HOME, else no home directory | `session.vibe` `settingsDir` | `settingsBase` (signinDecision) |
| A post's reply child reserved for another post conflicts | `ActionDirectory.vibe` submit | `reservedByOther` (actionsDecision) |
| A batch's outcome (read, wrote, done); the export finishes on done | `publish.vibe` `batchStep`, `pacedExport` | `batchOutcome` (exportDecision) |
| An empty history exports nothing | `publish.vibe` `batch` | `emptyHistory` |
| A round that wrote objects published, else current | `publish.vibe` `runPublish` | `publishOutcome` |

`agentFirst` also fixes the comparator for a login compared with itself (it answered -1 for the agent against the
agent; now `compared`, 0), which GitHub's unique assignee logins never reached. `wire.vibe` had a record saying browser
code may not import protocolDecision; nothing forbids it (`routes.vibe` already does), so it now calls the proved rule.
